nodes.name: minor
nodes.statement: A graph $H$ is a \defn{minor} of a graph $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by deleting vertices and edges, and by contracting edges.

nodes.name: Hadwiger number
nodes.statement: The maximum integer $n$ such that the complete graph $K_n$ is a minor of $G$ is called the \defn{Hadwiger number} of $G$, denoted \defn{$\mathrm{had}(G)$}.

nodes.name: proper colouring
nodes.statement: A \defn{proper colouring} of a graph $G$ assigns a colour to each vertex so that adjacent vertices receive distinct colours.

nodes.name: chromatic number
nodes.statement: The \defn{chromatic number} of $G$, denoted \defn{$\chi(G)$}, is the minimum integer $k$ such that $G$ has a proper colouring with $k$ colours.

nodes.name: Hadwiger's Conjecture
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$. Equivalently, if $G$ is $K_t$ minor-free, then $G$ is $(t-1)$-colourable.
nodes.label: conj:hc

nodes.name: independent set
nodes.statement: An \defn{independent set} in a graph $G$ is a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices in $G$.

nodes.name: independence number
nodes.statement: The \defn{independence number} of $G$, denoted \defn{$\alpha(G)$}, is the cardinality of the largest independent set in $G$.

nodes.name: Independence number weakening of Hadwiger's Conjecture
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/\alpha(G)$.
nodes.label: conj:indep

nodes.name: Duchet-Meyniel Theorem
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/ (2\alpha(G) -1)$.
nodes.label: thm:dm

nodes.name: Balogh-Kostochka bound
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/((2-c)\alpha(G))$, where $c = 1/19.2$.
nodes.label: thm:complete_minors_indep_no

nodes.name: $\mathrm{HC}_{\alpha = 2}$
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$.
nodes.label: conj:hc_chi

nodes.name: $\mathrm{HC}_{n/2}$
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/2$.
nodes.label: conj:hc_half

nodes.name: Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft properties of a minimum counterexample
nodes.statement:
\citet{PST03} proved that a minimum counterexample (in terms of $|V(G)|$) to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi} has several properties (see \cref{tab:minimal_properties}). In particular, they proved that if $G$ is a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, then $\mathrm{diam}(\overline{G}) = 2$, and $G$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_half}.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{HC}_{\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ satisfies $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant (\frac{1}{3} + \varepsilon) |V(G)|$.
nodes.label: conj:hc_epsilon

nodes.name: adjacent (sets of vertices)
nodes.statement: For disjoint subsets $A, B \subseteq V(G)$, $A$ and $B$ are \defn{adjacent} if some vertex in $A$ is adjacent to some vertex in $B$, otherwise $A$ and $B$ are \defn{non-adjacent}.

nodes.name: $V(M)$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{V(M)} := \{ v \in V(G) : \text{$v$ is an endpoint of an edge $e \in M$} \}$.

nodes.name: $V(e)$
nodes.statement: For an edge $e \in E(G)$, let $\mathdefn{V(e)}:= V(\{e\})$.

nodes.name: connected matching
nodes.statement: A matching $M \subseteq E(G)$ is \defn{connected} if for every two edges $e, f \in M$, $V(e)$ and $V(f)$ are adjacent.
differentia: for every two edges $e, f \in M$, $V(e)$ and $V(f)$ are adjacent

nodes.name: dominating matching
nodes.statement: A matching $M \subseteq E(G)$ is \defn{dominating} if each vertex of $V(G) \setminus V(M)$ is adjacent to each edge $e \in M$.
differentia: each vertex of $V(G) \setminus V(M)$ is adjacent to each edge $e \in M$

nodes.name: dominating edge
nodes.statement: An edge $xy \in E(G)$ is \defn{dominating} if $N_G(x) \cup N_G(y) = V(G)$. Equivalently, an edge $xy$ is dominating if $\{xy\}$ is a connected dominating matching of size $1$.

nodes.name: Linear-CM
nodes.statement: There is a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has a connected matching of size at least $c|V(G)|$.
conclusions: has a connected matching of size at least $c|V(G)|$
nodes.label: conj:linear_cm

nodes.name: Equivalence of Linear-CM and HC_epsilon (Thomasse)
nodes.statement: Thomass\'e first noted that \nameref{conj:linear_cm} and \nameref{conj:hc_epsilon} are equivalent (see \citep{furedi2005connected}).

nodes.name: 4-CM
nodes.statement: For every integer $t \geqslant 1$, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ with at least $4t - 1$ vertices has a connected matching of size at least $t$.
assumptions: every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ with at least $4t - 1$ vertices
conclusions: has a connected matching of size at least $t$
nodes.label: conj:4-CM

nodes.name: Tightness of 4t-1 in 4-CM
nodes.statement: The bound $4t - 1$ is best possible, since the disjoint union of two copies of the complete graph $K_{2t - 1}$ does not have a connected matching of size $t$.

nodes.name: Cambie: HC_{alpha=2} implies 4-CM
nodes.statement: Somewhat surprisingly, \citet{cambie2021hadwiger} proved that \nameref{conj:hc_chi} implies \nameref{conj:4-CM}.

nodes.name: model
nodes.statement: A \defn{model} of a graph $H$ in a graph $G$ is a function $\eta: V(H) \to 2^{V(G)}$ assigning the vertices of $H$ vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of $G$, such that if $uv \in E(H)$, then there is an edge of $G$ between $\eta(u)$ and $\eta(v)$.

nodes.name: branch set
nodes.statement: The sets $\{\eta(u): u \in V(H)\}$ are called the \defn{branch sets} of the model.

nodes.name: Models characterise minors
nodes.statement: There exists a model of a graph $H$ in $G$ if and only if $H$ is a minor of $G$.
conclusions: There exists a model of a graph $H$ in $G$ if and only if $H$ is a minor of $G$
equivalent_conditions: There exists a model of a graph $H$ in $G$

nodes.name: $\mathrm{SHC}_{\alpha = 2}$ (Seymour's strengthening of Hadwiger's Conjecture)
nodes.statement: Every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has a $K_{\chi(G)}$-model in which each branch set has size at most $2$.
conclusions: has a $K_{\chi(G)}$-model in which each branch set has size at most $2$
nodes.label: conj:shc_chi

nodes.name: $\mathrm{SHC}_{n/2}$
nodes.statement: Every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has a $K_{\ceil{|V(G)|/2}}$-model in which each branch set has size at most $2$.
conclusions: has a $K_{\ceil{|V(G)|/2}}$-model in which each branch set has size at most $2$
nodes.label: conj:shc_half

nodes.name: CDM (connected dominating matching conjecture)
nodes.statement: Every connected graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has a non-empty connected dominating matching.
conclusions: has a non-empty connected dominating matching
nodes.label: conj:cdm

nodes.name: Computational verification of CDM up to 11 vertices
nodes.statement: We have computationally verified \nameref{conj:cdm} for all graphs up to $11$ vertices.
conclusions: \nameref{conj:cdm} for all graphs up to $11$ vertices

nodes.name: Connectedness is needed in CDM
nodes.statement: Note that one cannot remove the assumption that $G$ is connected in \nameref{conj:cdm}, since the disjoint union of two non-empty complete graphs does not have a non-empty connected dominating matching.

nodes.name: inflation
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a graph and assign to each vertex $x \in V(H)$ an integer $c_x \geqslant 0$. Construct a new graph $G$ from $H$ by replacing each vertex $x \in V(H)$ with a clique $C_x$ of order $c_x$. Each vertex of $C_x$ is adjacent to each vertex of $C_y$ if and only if $xy \in E(H)$, otherwise $C_x$ and $C_y$ are non-adjacent. We call $G$ an \defn{inflation} of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Inflation of $H$: replace each vertex $x$ by a clique $C_x$ of size $c_x\ge 0$, cliques adjacent iff the vertices are adjacent.
differentia: replacing each vertex $x \in V(H)$ with a clique $C_x$ of order $c_x$

nodes.name: projection map
nodes.statement: We define the \defn{projection} map $\mathdefn{p}: V(G) \to V(H)$ by $p(v) = x$ if $v \in C_x$.

nodes.name: k-uniform and proper inflation
nodes.statement: An inflation of $H$ is \defn{$k$-uniform} if $c_x = k$ for each $x \in V(H)$, and \defn{proper} if $c_x \geqslant 1$ for each $x \in V(H)$.

nodes.name: Projection is surjective iff proper inflation
nodes.statement: Note that $p$ is surjective if and only if $G$ is a proper inflation of $H$.
conclusions: $p$ is surjective if and only if $G$ is a proper inflation of $H$

nodes.name: adjacent-twins
nodes.statement: Two vertices $u, v \in V(G)$ are \defn{adjacent-twins} if $uv \in E(G)$ and $N_G(u) \setminus \{v\} = N_G(v) \setminus \{u\}$.

nodes.name: adjacent-twin-free
nodes.statement: $G$ is \defn{adjacent-twin-free} if there are no adjacent-twins.

nodes.name: Unique smallest inflation base
nodes.statement: Observe that for every graph $G$, there is a unique smallest induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ such that $G$ is a proper inflation of $H$.
conclusions: there is a unique smallest induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ such that $G$ is a proper inflation of $H$

nodes.name: Proper inflations preserve alpha and complement diameter
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a proper inflation of $H$, then $\alpha(G) = \alpha(H)$ and $\mathrm{diam}(\overline{G}) = \mathrm{diam}(\overline{H})$.
nodes.label: obs:preserve

nodes.name: Inflations of alpha-2 graphs have alpha at most 2
nodes.statement: By \cref{obs:preserve}, if a graph $H$ has $\alpha(H) = 2$, then any inflation $G$ of $H$ also has $\alpha(G) \leqslant 2$.

nodes.name: Inflation conjecture
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, and suppose $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$, where $ \mathfrak{C} \in \{	ext{
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, 
ameref{conj:hc_epsilon}, 
ameref{conj:linear_cm}, 
ameref{conj:4-CM}, 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:shc_half}, 
ameref{conj:cdm}}\}. $ Then any inflation of $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.
nodes.label: conj:inflation

nodes.name: Catlin's counterexamples to Hajos' Conjecture
nodes.statement: \citet{Catlin79} showed that uniform inflations of the $5$-cycle are counterexamples to Hajós' Conjecture, which asserts that a graph with chromatic number $k$ contains $K_k$ as a topological minor.
conclusions: uniform inflations of the $5$-cycle are counterexamples to Hajós' Conjecture

nodes.name: blow-up
nodes.statement: $\overline{G}$ is a \defn{blow-up} of $\overline{H}$ if $G$ is an inflation of $H$. More precisely, if $G$ is an inflation of $H$ with $x \in V(H)$ replaced with a clique $C_x$ of order $c_x \geqslant 0$, then $\overline{G}$ is obtained from $\overline{H}$ by replacing each vertex $x \in V(\overline{H})$ with an independent set $A_x$ of order $c_x$ (so that each vertex of $A_x$ is adjacent to each vertex of $A_y$ if and only if $xy \in E(\overline{H})$). We use natural analogues of the terms \defn{proper}, \defn{$k$-uniform} and the \defn{projection} map for blow-ups.
nodes.statement_short: The complement of an inflation is a blow-up: vertices replaced by independent sets.

nodes.name: twins
nodes.statement: Two vertices $u, v \in V(G)$ are \defn{twins} if $uv \notin E(G)$ and $N_G(u) = N_G(v)$.

nodes.name: twin-free
nodes.statement: $G$ is \defn{twin-free} if no two vertices of $G$ are twins.

nodes.name: Adjacent-twin-free iff complement twin-free
nodes.statement: $G$ is adjacent-twin-free if and only if $\overline{G}$ is twin-free.
conclusions: $G$ is adjacent-twin-free if and only if $\overline{G}$ is twin-free

nodes.name: $\binom{[n]}{k}$
nodes.statement: For integers $n, k \geqslant 1$, let \defn{$\binom{[n]}{k}$} denote all $k$-subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$.

nodes.name: $K(n,k,\geqslant t)$
nodes.statement: For $t \geqslant 1$, let $K(n,k, \geqslant t)$ be the graph with vertex set $V(G) = \binom{[n]}{k}$, where two vertices are adjacent if and only if their corresponding subsets intersect in at least $t$ elements.
also_stated_at: For integers $n,k,t \geqslant 1$, let \defn{$K(n,k,\geqslant t)$} be the graph with vertex set $\binom{[n]}{k}$, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if their corresponding subsets intersect in at least $t$ elements.

nodes.name: Kneser graph
nodes.statement: Define $K(n,k, \leqslant t):= \overline{K(n,k, \geqslant t+1)}$ and $K(n,k,\leqslant 0):= K(n,k)$, known as the \defn{Kneser graph}.

nodes.name: generalised Kneser graph
nodes.statement: The graph $K(n, k, \leqslant t)$ is known as a \defn{generalised Kneser graph} in the literature.
also_stated_at: The graph $K(n, k, \leqslant t)$ is known as a \defn{generalised Kneser graph} in the literature.

nodes.name: minimal counterexample
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is a \defn{minimal counterexample} to $\mathfrak{C}$ if $G$ is a counterexample to $\mathfrak{C}$, but any proper induced subgraph of $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.
differentia: any proper induced subgraph of $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$

nodes.name: minimum counterexample
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is a \defn{minimum counterexample} to $\mathfrak{C}$ if $G$ is a counterexample to $\mathfrak{C}$, but every graph $H$ with $|V(H)| < |V(G)|$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.

nodes.name: clique number, matching number, connectivity, minimum degree, diameter
nodes.statement: We use $\mathdefn{\omega(G)}$ to denote the \defn{clique number}, $\mathdefn{\mu(G)}$ to denote the \defn{matching number}, $\mathdefn{\kappa(G)}$ to denote the \defn{vertex-connectivity}, $\mathdefn{\delta(G)}$ to denote the \defn{minimum degree}, and $\mathdefn{\mathrm{diam}(G)}$ to denote the \defn{diameter} of $G$.

nodes.name: distance
nodes.statement: For distinct $u, v \in V(G)$, let \defn{$\mathrm{dist}_G(u,v)$} denote the \defn{distance} between $u$ and $v$ in $G$.

nodes.name: neighbourhood
nodes.statement: For a vertex $v \in V(G)$, let \defn{$N_G(v)$} denote the set of neighbours of $v$ in $G$.

nodes.name: induced subgraph
nodes.statement: For a subset $S \subseteq V(G)$, let \defn{$G[S]$} be the subgraph of $G$ induced by $S$.

nodes.name: vertex deletion
nodes.statement: Let \defn{$G - S$} be the graph obtained from $G$ by deleting vertices of $S$ from $G$.

nodes.name: vertex and edge deletion/addition notation
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{G - v}$ denote $G - \{v\}$, and for an edge $xy \in E(G)$, let $\mathdefn{G - xy}$ (resp. $\mathdefn{G + xy}$) be the graph obtained by deleting (resp. adding) $xy$ from $G$.

nodes.name: complement
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{\overline{G}}$ denote the \defn{complement} of $G$.

nodes.name: Chromatic number via complement matching
nodes.statement: For each graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $\chi(G) = |V(G)| - \mu(\overline{G})$.
nodes.statement_short: If $\alpha(G)=2$ then $\chi(G)=|V(G)|-\mu(\overline{G})$.
nodes.label: lem:chromatic_matching

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: $\chi(G) \geqslant |V(G)| - \mu(\overline{G})$: Let $k:= \chi(G)$ and colour $G$ with $k$ colours. Since $\alpha(G) = 2$, each colour class has $1$ or $2$ vertices. Suppose $\ell$ of the colour classes have size $2$ and $m$ of the colour classes have size $1$. Thus, $k = \ell + m$ and $|V(G)| = 2\ell + m = \ell + k$. The colour classes of size $2$ correspond to a matching in $\overline{G}$, so $\ell \leqslant \mu(\overline{G})$. However, $\ell = |V(G)| - k = |V(G)| - \chi(G)$, so $|V(G)| - \chi(G) \leqslant \mu(\overline{G})$ and $\chi(G) \geqslant |V(G)| - \mu(\overline{G})$. $\chi(G) \leqslant |V(G)| - \mu(\overline{G})$: Let $M$ be the maximum matching in $\overline{G}$, and let $\ell = |M| = \mu(\overline{G})$. Let $m$ be the number of vertices in $V(G) \setminus V(M)$, so $|V(G)|= 2 \ell + m$. Use $\ell$ colours to colour $V(M)$ so that the endpoints of each edge of $M$ share the same colour, and endpoints of distinct edges receive distinct colours. Use $m$ different colours for each vertex in $V(G) \setminus V(M)$. This gives a proper colouring of $V(G)$ using $\ell + m$ colours. Therefore, $\chi(G) \leqslant k = \ell + m = |V(G)| - \mu(\overline{G})$.
nodes.statement_short: Two inequalities: colour classes of size 2 give a matching in the complement, and a maximum complement matching gives a colouring.

nodes.name: Polynomial-time chromatic number for alpha=2
nodes.statement: Since $\mu(\overline{G})$ can be computed in polynomial time \citep{Edmonds65a}, \cref{lem:chromatic_matching} implies that one can find the chromatic number of a graph with independence number $2$ in polynomial time.

nodes.name: vertex-critical
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is \defn{vertex-critical} if $\chi(G - v) < \chi(G)$ for each $v \in V(G)$.

nodes.name: k-critical
nodes.statement: For an integer $k \geqslant 1$, a vertex-critical graph with $\chi(G) = k$ is called \defn{$k$-critical}.

nodes.name: decomposable
nodes.statement: A graph is \defn{decomposable} if $V(G)$ can be partitioned into two non-empty subsets $A$ and $B$ such that each vertex of $A$ is adjacent to each vertex of $B$. Equivalently, $G$ is decomposable if the complement $\overline{G}$ is disconnected.

nodes.name: Gallai's theorem on critical graphs
nodes.statement: Every vertex-critical graph $G$ with $|V(G)| < 2\chi(G) - 1$ is decomposable.
nodes.label: thm:deep_theorem_of_gallai

nodes.name: Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft clique bound
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$. Then $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant (\omega(G) + |V(G)|) / 3$. Further, for any integer $k \geqslant 1$, if $|V(G)| \geqslant 2k - 1$ and $\omega(G) \geqslant k - 2$, then $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant k$.
nodes.label: lem:first_seagull

nodes.name: Deleting two non-adjacent vertices of a critical graph
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, and suppose $G$ is $k$-critical with $|V(G)| = 2k - 1$. Then the graph $G'$ obtained by deleting two non-adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$ is $(k-1)$-critical.
conclusions: the graph $G'$ obtained by deleting two non-adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$  is $(k-1)$-critical
nodes.label: lem:non_adj_vtx_crit

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.8
nodes.statement: Let $G' := G - x - y$. Since $G$ is $k$-critical, $\chi(G') \leqslant \chi(G - x) \leqslant k -1$. If $\chi(G') \leqslant k -2$, then by assigning a new colour to $x$ and $y$, we obtain a proper colouring of $G$ with $k-1$ colours, so $\chi(G) \leqslant k -1$, a contradiction. Hence, $\chi(G') = k-1$. We prove that $G'$ is $(k-1)$-critical. Suppose to the contrary. Then there is a vertex $u \in V(G')$ such that $\chi(G' -u) = k-1$. Since $G$ is vertex-critical, $\chi(G - u) = k-1$. Since $\chi(G' - u) = k - 1$ and $|V(G' - u)| = 2k - 4$, by \cref{lem:chromatic_matching}, $\mu(\overline{G' - u}) = 2k - 4 - (k-1) = k- 3$. Therefore, $\mu(\overline{G - u}) = k - 2$. By \cref{lem:chromatic_matching}, $\chi(G - u) = 2k - 2- (k-2) = k$. This contradicts the assumption that $G$ is $k$-critical.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\chi(G')=k-1$, then contradiction via Lemma 2.5 if some vertex deletion keeps $\chi(G'-u)=k-1$.

nodes.name: Equivalent conditions for edge-maximal triangle-free graphs
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent for a triangle-free graph $G$ with ${|V(G)| \geqslant 3}$: \begin{enumerate}[(\alph*)] \item $G$ is edge-maximal triangle-free (that is, for any edge $xy \in E(\overline{G})$, $G + xy$ contains a triangle), \item $G$ has diameter $2$, \item $\overline{G}$ is edge-minimal with $\alpha(\overline{G}) = 2$ (that is, for any $xy \in E(\overline{G})$, $\alpha(\overline{G} - xy) = 3$), \item $\overline{G}$ does not contain a dominating edge. \end{enumerate}
equivalent_conditions: $G$ is edge-maximal triangle-free (that is, for any edge $xy \in E(\overline{G})$,  $G + xy$ contains a triangle)
$\overline{G}$ is edge-minimal with $\alpha(\overline{G}) = 2$ (that is, for any $xy \in E(\overline{G})$, $\alpha(\overline{G} - xy) = 3$)
$\overline{G}$ does not contain a dominating edge
nodes.label: lem:equiv_triangle_free

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: (a) $\Rightarrow $ (b): Say $G$ is edge-maximal triangle-free. If $\mathrm{diam}(G) = 1$, then $G$ is complete, contradicting the assumption that $G$ is triangle-free since $|V(G)| \geqslant 3$. So $\mathrm{diam}(G)\neq 1$. Suppose for the sake of contradiction that $\mathrm{diam}(G) \geqslant 3$. Let $v$ and $w$ be vertices at distance at least $3$ in $G$. So $v$ and $w$ have no common neighbour. Then $G + vw$ is triangle-free, contradicting the edge-maximality of $G$. Thus, $\mathrm{diam}(G) = 2$. (b) $\Rightarrow $ (c): Say $G$ has diameter 2. So $G$ is connected, and any two non-adjacent vertices in $G$ have a common neighbour. Since $G$ is connected, $|E(G)| \neq 0$, implying that $\alpha(\overline{G}) > 1$. Since $G$ is triangle-free, $\alpha(\overline{G}) = 2$. In $\overline{G}$, any two adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$ have a common non-neighbour $u \in V(G)$. Then $\alpha(\overline{G} - xy) = 3$, since $\{x,y,u\}$ is an independent set in $\overline{G} - xy$. (c) $\Rightarrow$ (d): Let $xy \in E(\overline{G})$. Since $\alpha(\overline{G}) = 2$ and $\alpha(\overline{G} - xy) = 3$, there is an independent set $S$ of size $3$ in $\overline{G} - xy$ containing $x$ and $y$. Let $u$ be the other element of $S$. In $\overline{G}$, $u$ is not adjacent to $x$ and $y$, and hence $xy$ is not a dominating edge. (d) $\Rightarrow$ (a): Since $\overline{G}$ does not contain a dominating edge, in $G$, any two non-adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$ have a common neighbour $u \in V(G)$. Then $G + xy$ contains a triangle $uxy$, which proves (a).
nodes.statement_short: Cyclic chain of implications (a)$\Rightarrow$(b)$\Rightarrow$(c)$\Rightarrow$(d)$\Rightarrow$(a).

nodes.name: Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft connectivity theorem
nodes.statement: Every connected graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $\kappa(G) \leqslant |V(G)| / 2$ has a non-empty connected dominating matching.
conclusions: has a non-empty connected dominating matching
nodes.label: thm:connectivity

nodes.name: Justification of Observation 2.11
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, the non-neighbours of each vertex induce a complete graph.
nodes.statement_short: Non-neighbours of a vertex form a clique when $\alpha=2$.

nodes.name: Minimum degree bound for alpha=2
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, we have $\delta(G) \geqslant |V(G)| - 1 - \omega(G)$.
nodes.label: obs:non-neighbours

nodes.name: Properties of minimal and minimum counterexamples
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$. With reference to \cref{tab:minimal_properties}:  egin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2em] \item If $G$ is a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, then $G$ satisfies Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:proper_minor_less_chi})}. \item If $G$ is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, then $G$ satisfies Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:ABC_sizes})}. \item If $G$ is a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, then $G$ satisfies Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:C5_condition})}. \item If $G$ is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, then $G$ satisfies Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:C5_condition})}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Minimal/minimum counterexamples to HC and SHC for $\alpha=2$ satisfy the structural properties listed in Table 1.
nodes.label: thm:minimal_properties

nodes.name: Part (a) is due to Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft
nodes.statement: Note that (a) was shown by \citet{PST03}, which is implied by Properties \textup{(\ref{prop:vertex_critical})} -- \textup{(\ref{prop:ABC_sizes})} of (b), since a minimum counterexample to \nameref{conj:hc_chi} is a minimal counterexample to \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.12
nodes.statement:
First, we prove (d). Let $G$ be a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}. Recall that \defn{$\mathrm{had}_2(G)$} is the order of the largest complete graph model of $G$ such that each branch set has one or two vertices. So $\mathrm{had}_2(G) < \chi(G)$ but $\mathrm{had}_2(H) \geqslant \chi(H)$ for every proper induced subgraph $H$ of $G$.  egin{enumerate}[label={}, leftmargin=0em, itemsep=1.5pt] \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})}: Since $G$ is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) < \chi(G)$, and for each vertex $v \in V(G)$, $\mathrm{had}_2(G - v) \geqslant \chi(G - v)$. Since $\mathrm{had}_2(G - v) \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G)$, we have $\chi(G - v) \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G - v) \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G) < \chi(G)$, so $\chi(G - v) < \chi(G)$. Thus $G$ is vertex-critical. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:not_decomposable})}: Suppose $G$ is decomposable. Then $V(G) = A \cup B$, where $A \cap B = \varnothing$, $A 
eq \varnothing$ and $B 
eq \varnothing$, and each vertex of $A$ is adjacent to each vertex of $B$. Since $G$ is a minimal counterexample, $\mathrm{had}_2(G[A]) \geqslant \chi(G[A])$ and $\mathrm{had}_2(G[B]) \geqslant \chi(G[B])$. However, since each vertex of $A$ is adjacent to each vertex of $B$, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G[A]) + \mathrm{had}_2(G[B])$ and $\chi(G) = \chi(G[A]) + \chi(G[B])$. Hence, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$, a contradiction. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}: Since $\alpha(G) = 2$, $|V(G)| \leqslant 2 \chi(G)$ and $|V(G -v)| \leqslant 2 \chi(G - v)$ for each vertex $v \in V(G)$. If $\left|V(G)ight| = 2 \chi(G)$, then by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})}, $ 2\chi(G) - 1 = \left|V(G - v)ight| \leqslant 2\chi(G - v) = 2 (\chi(G) - 1) = 2\chi(G) - 2$, a contradiction. Therefore, $|V(G)| \leqslant 2 \chi(G) - 1$. If $|V(G)| < 2 \chi(G) - 1$, then by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} and \cref{thm:deep_theorem_of_gallai}, $G$ is decomposable, contradicting Property 	extup{(ef{prop:not_decomposable})}. Thus, $|V(G)| = 2\chi(G) - 1$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:subgraph_vertex_critical})}: Follows from Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} and \cref{lem:non_adj_vtx_crit}. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:complement_minus_x_pm})}: Let $v \in V(G)$ and let $G' = G - v$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}, $|V(G)| = 2\chi(G) - 1$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})}, $\chi(G') = \chi(G) - 1$. By \cref{lem:chromatic_matching}, $ \mu(\overline{G}') = |V(G')| - \chi(G') = 2 \chi(G) - 2 - (\chi(G) - 1) = \chi(G) - 1 =  rac{1}{2} |V(G')|$, and hence $\overline{G}'$ has a perfect matching. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_connected_dominating_matching})}: Suppose $G$ has a non-empty connected dominating matching $M$ with $t \geqslant 1$ edges. Let $G' = G - V(M)$, which by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} has $2(\chi(G)-t) - 1$ vertices. This implies $ \chi(G') \geqslant  rac{|V(G')|}{\alpha(G')} \geqslant  rac{2(\chi(G)-t) - 1}{2} = \chi(G) -t -  rac{1}{2} $. Since $\chi(G')$ is an integer, $\chi(G') \geqslant \chi(G) -t$. Since $G'$ is a proper induced subgraph of $G$, $\mathrm{had}_2(G') \geqslant \chi(G') \geqslant \chi(G) -t$. However, each edge of $M$ is adjacent to each vertex of $G'$, implying that $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G') + t$. Consequently, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$, a contradiction. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_dominating_edges})}: By Property~	extup{(ef{prop:no_connected_dominating_matching})}, $G$ has no dominating edge. The result follows from \cref{lem:equiv_triangle_free}. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:kappa_geq_chi})}: By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_connected_dominating_matching})} and \cref{thm:connectivity}, $\kappa(G) > |V(G)|/2$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}, $\kappa(G) > (2\chi(G) - 1)/2 = \chi(G) - 1/2$. Since $\kappa(G)$ is an integer, $\kappa(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:delta_geq_chi})}: For every graph $G$, $\delta(G) \geqslant \kappa(G)$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:kappa_geq_chi})}, $\kappa(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:hamiltonian})}: From Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} and 	extup{(ef{prop:delta_geq_chi})}, $\delta(G)\geqslant \chi(G) = (|V(G)| + 1)/2$. By Dirac's Theorem \citep{Dirac52a}, $G$ is Hamiltonian. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:factor_critical})}: Let $v \in V(G)$ be any vertex. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}, $|V(G -v)|$ is even. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:hamiltonian})}, $G - v$ has a Hamiltonian path $P$. We obtain a perfect matching of $G -v$ by taking alternating edges in $P$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:complement_diameter_2})}: By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_dominating_edges})} and \cref{lem:equiv_triangle_free}, $\mathrm{diam}(\overline{G}) = 2$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:B_nonempty})}: Let $xy \in E(\overline{G})$. Let $B:= N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$, $A:= N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)$ and $C:= N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x)$. Since $\alpha(G) = 2$, $A$ and $C$ are cliques. Suppose $B = \varnothing$. Then $|A| \geqslant (|V(G)| - 2) / 2$ or $|C| \geqslant (|V(G)| - 2) / 2$. However, then $A \cup \{ x \}$ or $C \cup \{ y \}$ is a clique with at least $|V(G)|/2$ vertices. Therefore, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/2$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant (2\chi(G) - 1)/2 = \chi(G) - 1/2$. Since $\mathrm{had}_2(G)$ is an integer, $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$. However, then $G$ is not a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, a contradiction. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:B_non_neighbours})}: Let $xy \in E(\overline{G})$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_dominating_edges})}, $xb$ is not a dominating edge, and there is a vertex $c$ adjacent to neither $x$ nor $b$. Since $\alpha(G) = 2$, $N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)$ and $N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x)$ are cliques in $G$, so $b 
otin (N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)) \cup (N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x))$. Since $xy 
otin E(G)$, $V(G) \setminus \{x, y\} = N_G(x) \cup N_G(y)$, and hence $b \in N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:C5_condition})}: Let $xy \in E(\overline{G})$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:B_nonempty})}, there is a vertex $b \in N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:B_non_neighbours})}, there is a vertex $a \in N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)$ not adjacent to $b$ and a vertex $c \in N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x)$ not adjacent to $b$. ameref{conj:shc_chi} is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, and therefore Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:C5_condition})} also hold for minimum counterexamples to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}. This completes the proof of (c). By replacing $\mathrm{had}_2(G)$ with $\mathrm{had}(G)$, the same arguments show that Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:vertex_critical})} -- 	extup{(ef{prop:C5_condition})} hold for minimal and minimum counterexamples to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. In what follows, we prove the remaining properties for (b). Let $G$ be a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}.  egin{enumerate}[label={}, leftmargin=0em, itemsep=1.5pt] \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:chi_at_least_7})}: \citet{RST-Comb93} proved Hadwiger's Conjecture for $K_6$ minor-free graphs. Consequently, since $G$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, $\chi(G) > \mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant 6$. Thus $\chi(G) \geqslant 7$. (Note that this argument fails for 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}.) \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:kappa_at_least_7})}: This follows from Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:kappa_geq_chi})} and 	extup{(ef{prop:chi_at_least_7})}. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:omega_at_most_chi_minus_3})}: Follows from Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} and \cref{lem:first_seagull} (with $k = \chi(G)$). \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:delta_geq_chi_plus_1})}: By \cref{obs:non-neighbours}, $\delta(G) \geqslant |V(G)| - 1 - \omega(G)$. By Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} and 	extup{(ef{prop:omega_at_most_chi_minus_3})}: $|V(G)| - 1 - \omega(G) \geqslant 2 \chi(G) - 2 - (\chi(G) - 3) = \chi(G) + 1$. Hence, $\delta(G) \geqslant \chi(G) + 1$. \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:ABC_sizes})}: Let $xy \in E(\overline{G})$. The set $(N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)) \cup \{x\}$ is a clique in $G$, so by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:omega_at_most_chi_minus_3})}, $|(N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)) \cup \{x\}| \leqslant \chi(G) - 3$. Thus, $|N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)| \leqslant \chi(G) -4$. Similarly, $|N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x)| \leqslant \chi(G) -4$. We deduce that $|N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)| \geqslant 2\chi(G) - 3 - 2(\chi(G) - 4) = 5$. By Properties 	extup{(ef{prop:B_nonempty})} and 	extup{(ef{prop:B_non_neighbours})}, $N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y) 
eq \varnothing$. Suppose $|N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)| = 1$, and let $a \in N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)$. Then by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:B_non_neighbours})}, each vertex $b \in N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$ is not adjacent to $a$. $N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$ are non-neighbours of $a$, and since $\alpha(G) = 2$, $N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)$ is a clique. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:delta_geq_chi_plus_1})}, $|N_G(x)| \geqslant \chi(G) + 1$, so $|N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)| \geqslant \chi(G)$. This contradicts Property 	extup{(ef{prop:omega_at_most_chi_minus_3})}. Thus, $|N_G(x) \setminus N_G(y)| \geqslant 2$. Similarly, $|N_G(y) \setminus N_G(x)| \geqslant 2$. We deduce that $|N_G(x) \cap N_G(y)| \leqslant |V(G-x-y)| - 4 = 2\chi(G) - 3 - 4 = 2\chi(G) - 7$. \end{enumerate} This completes the proof of (b). It remains to show (a), which was shown by \citet{PST03}. We include the proof for completeness. Let $G$ be a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. A graph $H$ is an \defn{induced minor} of $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by a sequence of vertex deletions and edge contractions.  egin{obs} \phantom{linebreaker}  egin{itemize} \item $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if and only if there is a model $\eta: V(H) 	o 2^{V(G)}$ of $H$ in $G$ such that $uv \in E(H)$ if and only if there is an edge of $G$ between a vertex of $\eta(u)$ and a vertex of $\eta(v)$ \citep{InducedMinors24}. (This is called an \defn{induced minor model} in the literature.) \item If $H$ is an induced minor of $G$, then $\alpha(H) \leqslant \alpha(G)$. (If $\eta: V(H) 	o 2^{V(G)}$ is an induced minor model of $H$ in $G$, given an independent set $S \subseteq V(H)$, for each $x \in S$, choose a vertex $v_x \in \eta(x)$. Then $\{v_x: x \in S\}$ is an independent set in $G$.) \item If $H'$ is a minor of $G$, then there is an induced minor $H$ of $G$ such that $H'$ is a subgraph of $H$ with $V(H) = V(H')$. \end{itemize} \end{obs}  egin{enumerate}[label={}, leftmargin=0em, itemsep=1.5pt] \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:edge_critical})}: Let $xy \in E(G)$, and let $H$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by contracting $xy$ to a new vertex $z$. Then $H$ is an induced minor of $G$, and by \cref{obs:induced_minors}, $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$. Since $G$ is a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, $\mathrm{had}(H) \geqslant \chi(H)$ and $\mathrm{had}(G) < \chi(G)$. Since $\mathrm{had}(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(G)$, we have $\chi(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(G) < \chi(G)$, so $\chi(H) < \chi(G)$. Colour $H$ with $\chi(H)$ colours. We obtain a $\chi(H)$-colouring of $G - xy$ by colouring $x$ and $y$ (which are not adjacent) with the colour given to $z$. Consequently, $\chi(G - xy) < \chi(G)$. (Note that Property 	extup{(ef{prop:edge_critical})} may not be true for minimal counterexamples of 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, since the proof requires the contraction operation. Further Property 	extup{(ef{prop:edge_critical})} may not be true for minimum counterexamples to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, since $\mathrm{had}_2(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G)$ may not hold if $H$ is a minor of $G$. For example, $\mathrm{had}_2(C_7) = 2$, but $\mathrm{had}_2(K_3) = 3$.) \item Property 	extup{(ef{prop:proper_minor_less_chi})}: Let $H'$ be a proper minor of $G$. Suppose $|V(H')| < |V(G)|$. By \cref{obs:induced_minors}, there is an induced minor $H$ of $G$ such that $H'$ is a subgraph of $H$ with $V(H) = V(H')$. Since $G$ is a minimum counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, $\mathrm{had}(H) \geqslant \chi(H)$ and $\mathrm{had}(G) < \chi(G)$. Since $\mathrm{had}(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(G)$, we have $\chi(H') \leqslant \chi(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(H) \leqslant \mathrm{had}(G) < \chi(G)$. If $|V(H')| = |V(G)|$, then $H'$ is a subgraph of $G-xy$ for some edge $xy \in E(G)$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:edge_critical})}, $\chi(H') \leqslant \chi(G - xy) < \chi(G)$. In each case, $\chi(H') < \chi(G)$. \end{enumerate} This completes the proof of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}.
nodes.statement_short: Property-by-property verification for minimal SHC counterexamples (criticality, Gallai's theorem, Lemma 2.5), then HC-specific bounds, then contraction arguments for minimum counterexamples.

nodes.name: Facts about induced minors
nodes.statement: \phantom{linebreaker} \begin{itemize} \item $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if and only if there is a model $\eta: V(H) \to 2^{V(G)}$ of $H$ in $G$ such that $uv \in E(H)$ if and only if there is an edge of $G$ between a vertex of $\eta(u)$ and a vertex of $\eta(v)$ \citep{InducedMinors24}. (This is called an \defn{induced minor model} in the literature.) \item If $H$ is an induced minor of $G$, then $\alpha(H) \leqslant \alpha(G)$. (If $\eta: V(H) \to 2^{V(G)}$ is an induced minor model of $H$ in $G$, given an independent set $S \subseteq V(H)$, for each $x \in S$, choose a vertex $v_x \in \eta(x)$. Then $\{v_x: x \in S\}$ is an independent set in $G$.) \item If $H'$ is a minor of $G$, then there is an induced minor $H$ of $G$ such that $H'$ is a subgraph of $H$ with $V(H) = V(H')$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: If $H$ is an induced minor of $G$, then $\alpha(H) \leqslant \alpha(G)$.
If $H'$ is a minor of $G$, then there is an induced minor $H$ of $G$ such that $H'$ is a subgraph of $H$ with $V(H) = V(H')$.
