nodes.name: Equivalences and implications among HC variants
nodes.statement:
egin{itemize} \item 
ameref{conj:hc_chi} is equivalent to 
ameref{conj:hc_half}. More precisely, any counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_half} is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, and any minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi} is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_half} \citep{PST03}. \item 
ameref{conj:shc_chi} is equivalent to 
ameref{conj:shc_half}. More precisely, any counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_half} is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, and any minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi} is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_half}. \item 
ameref{conj:cdm} implies 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, which implies 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: HC$_{\alpha=2}\Leftrightarrow$HC$_{n/2}$, SHC$_{\alpha=2}\Leftrightarrow$SHC$_{n/2}$, and CDM$\Rightarrow$SHC$\Rightarrow$HC.
nodes.label: thm:equiv

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.14
nodes.statement:
egin{itemize} \item Let $G$ be a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}, $|V(G)| = 2\chi(G) - 1$. Since $G$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, $\mathrm{had}(G) < \chi(G) = (|V(G)| + 1)/2$. Since $|V(G)|$ is odd and $\mathrm{had}(G)$ is an integer, $\mathrm{had}(G) < |V(G)|/2$, so $G$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_half}. Conversely, if $G$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, then $\mathrm{had}(G) < |V(G)|/2 \leqslant \chi(G)$, so $G$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. \item We obtain the conclusion by replacing $\mathrm{had}(G)$ with $\mathrm{had}_2(G)$ in the above argument. \item It is straightforward to see that 
ameref{conj:shc_chi} implies 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. A minimal counterexample $G$ to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi} is connected, since otherwise $G$ is the disjoint union of two complete graphs. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_connected_dominating_matching})} of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}, $G$ does not have a non-empty connected dominating matching, and thus is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:cdm}. \qedhere \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Parity argument using $|V(G)|=2\chi(G)-1$ for minimal counterexamples; CDM via Property (6).

nodes.name: H-free
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is \defn{$H$-free} if $G$ does not contain $H$ as an induced subgraph.

nodes.name: C5-free characterisation via dominating edges
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ is $C_5$-free if and only if every connected induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ with $\alpha(H) = 2$ has a dominating edge.
conclusions: is $C_5$-free if and only if every connected induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ with $\alpha(H) = 2$ has a dominating edge
equivalent_conditions: every connected induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ with $\alpha(H) = 2$ has a dominating edge
nodes.label: thm:c5

nodes.name: Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft: C5-free graphs satisfy HC_{n/2}
nodes.statement: \citet*{PST03} instead proved that every $C_5$-free graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/ 2$.

nodes.name: Derivation of the Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft C5 result from Theorem 2.15
nodes.statement:
\cref{thm:c5} strengthens this result, as we now explain. Suppose $G$ is a $C_5$-free graph with $\mathrm{had}(G) < |V(G)|/2$ and $\alpha(G) = 2$. Thus, $G$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. Let $H$ be a minimal induced subgraph of $G$ that fails 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. By \cref{thm:equiv}, $H$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, and by Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_dominating_edges})} of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}, $H$ has no dominating edges. However, $H$ is $C_5$-free, so \cref{thm:c5} implies that $H$ has a dominating edge, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Take a minimal induced counterexample; it has no dominating edge by Theorem 2.12 but Theorem 2.15 gives one.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.15
nodes.statement: ($\Rightarrow $): Suppose $H$ is a connected induced subgraph of $G$ with no dominating edge. Since $\alpha(H) = 2$ and $H$ is connected, there are two vertices $x, y$ such that $\mathrm{dist}_H(x,y) = 2$. Let $b \in N_H(x) \cap N_H(y)$. The edge $xb \in E(H)$ is not dominating, so there is a vertex $c$ adjacent to neither $x$ nor $b$. Since $\alpha(H) = 2$ and $xy \notin E(H)$, $N_H(x) \cup N_H(y) = V(H)$. Therefore, $c \in N_H(y) \setminus N_H(x)$. Similarly, since $yb$ is not a dominating edge, there is a vertex $a \in N_H(x) \setminus N_H(y)$. If $ac \notin E(H)$, then $\{a,b,c\}$ is an independent set of size $3$, a contradiction. So $ac \in E(H)$. Then $xacyb$ is an induced $5$-cycle in $H$. Thus $G$ is not $C_5$-free. ($\Leftarrow $): $C_5$ is an induced subgraph of $G$ with no dominating edges.
nodes.statement_short: ($\Rightarrow$) a connected induced subgraph without dominating edge contains an induced $C_5$; ($\Leftarrow$) $C_5$ itself.

nodes.name: $B_7$
nodes.statement: Let \defn{$B_7$} be the graph shown in \cref{fig:b7}.

nodes.name: B7-free graphs have connected dominating matchings
nodes.statement: Every $B_7$-free connected graph $G$ with ${\alpha(G) = 2}$ has a non-empty connected dominating matching.
conclusions: has a non-empty connected dominating matching
nodes.label: thm:b7

nodes.name: Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft: B7-free graphs satisfy HC_{n/2}
nodes.statement: For \cref{thm:b7}, \citet*{PST03} proved instead that every $B_7$-free graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/ 2$.

nodes.name: C-unavoidable
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{C} \in \{	ext{
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:shc_half}, 
ameref{conj:cdm}}\}$. A graph $H$ with $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$ is \defn{$\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable} if every connected $H$-free graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$. Equivalently, $H$ is $\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable if any counterexample to $\mathfrak{C}$ contains $H$ as an induced subgraph.

nodes.name: Unavoidability is inherited by induced subgraphs
nodes.statement: Note that if $H$ is an induced subgraph of $H'$ and $H'$ is $\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable, then $H$ is $\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable.

nodes.name: Unavoidability implications among CDM, SHC and HC
nodes.statement:
By \cref{thm:equiv}, since 
ameref{conj:cdm} implies 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, and 
ameref{conj:shc_chi} implies 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, any 
ameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable graph is 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidable, and any 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidable graph is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable.

nodes.name: HC and HC_{n/2} unavoidability coincide
nodes.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$.  egin{itemize} \item $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable if and only if $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_half}-unavoidable. \item $H$ is 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidable if and only if $H$ is 
ameref{conj:shc_half}-unavoidable. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $H$ is \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable if and only if $H$ is \nameref{conj:hc_half}-unavoidable
$H$ is \nameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidable if and only if $H$ is \nameref{conj:shc_half}-unavoidable

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.17
nodes.statement:
Suppose $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable. Since 
ameref{conj:hc_chi} implies 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_half}-unavoidable. Conversely, suppose $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_half}-unavoidable, and suppose $H$ is not 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable. Let $G$ be an $H$-free graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ that fails 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. Let $G'$ be a minimal induced subgraph of $G$ such that $G'$ is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. Then $G'$ is $H$-free, and $\alpha(G') = 2$. Then $G'$ is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. By \cref{thm:equiv}, $G'$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_half}. This contradicts the assumption that $H$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_half}-unavoidable. The analogous equivalence of 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidability and 
ameref{conj:shc_half}-unavoidability follows a similar argument.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a minimal induced counterexample and apply Theorem 2.14.

nodes.name: Twin-freeness and preservation of H-freeness under inflation
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent for a graph $H$: \begin{enumerate}[(\alph*)] \item $H$ is adjacent-twin-free, \item $\overline{H}$ is twin-free, \item For any graph $G$, if $G$ is $H$-free, then any inflation $G'$ of $G$ is $H$-free, \item For any graph $G$, if $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free, then any blow-up $G'$ of $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free. \end{enumerate}
equivalent_conditions: For any graph $G$, if $G$ is $H$-free, then any inflation $G'$ of $G$ is $H$-free
For any graph $G$, if $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free, then any blow-up $G'$ of $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free
nodes.label: lem:blow_up_avoidant

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.18
nodes.statement: The equivalence of (a) and (b) is straightforward. The equivalence of (c) and (d) is straightforward. We show the equivalence of (b) and (d). (d) $\Rightarrow $ (b): Suppose $\overline{H}$ is not twin-free. Then there exists $uv \notin E(\overline{H})$ with $N_{\overline{H}}(u) = N_{\overline{H}}(v)$. Consider $G := \overline{H} - v$. Then $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free. However, since $N_{\overline{H}}(u) = N_{\overline{H}}(v)$, $\overline{H}$ is a blow-up of $G$ with $u \in V(\overline{H})$ replaced by an independent set of size $2$. This contradicts (d). (b) $\Rightarrow$ (d): Suppose (d) does not hold. Then there exists a graph $G$ and a blow-up $G'$ of $G$ such that $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free, but $G'$ is not $\overline{H}$-free. Let $p: V(G') \to V(G)$ be the projection map. Consider an induced subgraph $J$ of $G'$ isomorphic to $\overline{H}$. Since $G$ is $\overline{H}$-free, there are two non-adjacent vertices $v, v' \in V(J)$ with $p(v) = p(v')$; that is, $N_{G'}(v) = N_{G'}(v')$. However, $N_{\overline{H}}(v) = N_{G'}(v) \cap V(\overline{H}) = N_{G'}(v') \cap V(\overline{H}) = N_{\overline{H}}(v')$, so $\overline{H}$ is not twin-free.
nodes.statement_short: (a)$\Leftrightarrow$(b) and (c)$\Leftrightarrow$(d) are direct; prove (b)$\Leftrightarrow$(d) via twins and the projection map.

nodes.name: Adjacent-twin-free unavoidable graphs handle inflations
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{C} \in \{	ext{
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:shc_half}, 
ameref{conj:cdm}}\}$, and suppose $H$ is an adjacent-twin-free $\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable graph. If $G$ is a connected $H$-free graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, then any inflation of $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.
nodes.label: lem:unavoidable_adj_twin_free

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.19
nodes.statement: Since $H$ is adjacent-twin-free, by \cref{lem:blow_up_avoidant} and the assumption that $G$ is $H$-free, any inflation of $G$ is $H$-free. Since $H$ is $\mathfrak{C}$-unavoidable, any inflation of $G$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Inflations stay $H$-free by Lemma 2.18, so unavoidability applies.

nodes.name: Kriesell's conjecture on infinitely many unavoidable graphs
nodes.statement: \citet{Kriesell10} conjectured there are infinitely many \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable graphs.

nodes.name: B7 contains all 4-vertex alpha<=2 graphs except C4
nodes.statement: Except for the $4$-cycle $C_4$, $B_7$ contains every $4$-vertex graph with independence number at most $2$ as an induced subgraph.
conclusions: Except for the $4$-cycle $C_4$, $B_7$ contains every $4$-vertex graph with independence number at most $2$ as an induced subgraph

nodes.name: C4 is CDM-unavoidable
nodes.statement: \citet{PST03} showed that $C_4$ is \nameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable.

nodes.name: All graphs on at most 4 vertices are CDM-unavoidable
nodes.statement: Combined with \cref{thm:b7}, this implies that each graph $H$ with $|V(H)| \leqslant 4$ and $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$ is \nameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable.

nodes.name: Kriesell: graphs on at most 5 vertices are CDM-unavoidable
nodes.statement: \citet{Kriesell10} extended this result, proving that each graph $H$ with $|V(H)| \leqslant 5$ and $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$ is \nameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable.

nodes.name: Unavoidability of six-vertex graphs
nodes.statement: It is not known if every graph on six vertices is \nameref{conj:shc_chi}-unavoidable (or even \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable).

nodes.name: 5-wheel $W_5$
nodes.statement: For \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable graphs, let \defn{$W_5$} denote the $5$-wheel, obtained from the $5$-cycle by adding a vertex adjacent to each vertex of the $5$-cycle.

nodes.name: Bosse: W5 is HC-unavoidable
nodes.statement: \citet{Bosse19} proved that $W_5$ is \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable.

nodes.name: Carter's 33 HC-unavoidable graphs
nodes.statement: Using ideas from \citet{Bosse19}, \citet{Carter22} computationally proved that there is a list $H_1, \dots, H_{33}$ of \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable graphs, none of which contains another as an induced subgraph.
conclusions: there is a list $H_1, \dots, H_{33}$ of \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable graphs, none of which contains another as an induced subgraph

nodes.name: K8 and complement of K_{1,6} are HC-unavoidable
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, \citet{Carter22} proved that $K_8$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable, and \citet{Zhou23} proved that $\overline{K_{1,6}}$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable ootnote{\citet{Zhou23} actually proved that a different graph is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable (see Theorem 1.6, \citep{Zhou23}); however, that graph is an induced subgraph of one of \citet{Carter22}'s $33$ graphs.}.

nodes.name: All graphs of Table 2 are HC-unavoidable
nodes.statement: The joint results in \citep{Bosse19, Carter22, Zhou23,PST03} imply that each graph from \cref{tab:unavoidable_graphs} is \nameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable. Equivalently, if $G$ is a counterexample to \nameref{conj:hc_chi}, then $G$ contains every graph from \cref{tab:unavoidable_graphs} as an induced subgraph.
nodes.origin_citation: Bosse 2019; Carter 2022; Zhou 2023; Plummer, Stiebitz, Toft 2003

nodes.name: clique ratio
nodes.statement: This section summarises the literature on Hadwiger's Conjecture for graphs with large \defn{clique ratio}, defined for a graph $G$ to be $\omega(G) / |V(G)|$.

nodes.name: seagull
nodes.statement: A \defn{seagull} $S$ of a graph $G$ is an induced $3$-vertex-path of $G$.

nodes.name: Disjoint seagulls give complete minors
nodes.statement: If $\alpha(G) = 2$, then each vertex of $G - S$ is adjacent to $S$. Thus, if $G$ has $k$ vertex-disjoint seagulls, then $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant k$.
conclusions: each vertex of $G - S$ is adjacent to $S$

nodes.name: Chudnovsky-Seymour seagull theorem
nodes.statement: Let $k \geqslant 1$ be an integer and let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $G \ncong W_5$. Then $G$ has $k$ vertex-disjoint seagulls if and only if: \begin{enumerate} \item $|V(G)| \geqslant 3k$, \item $\kappa(G) \geqslant k$, \item For each clique $C \subseteq V(G)$, if $D$ is the set of vertices in $V(G) \setminus C$ that have both a neighbour and a non-neighbour in $C$, then $|D| + |V(G) \setminus C| \geqslant 2k$, and \item $\mu(\overline{G}) \geqslant k$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $G \ncong W_5$
conclusions: $G$ has $k$ vertex-disjoint seagulls if and only if
equivalent_conditions: For each clique $C \subseteq V(G)$, if $D$ is the set of vertices in $V(G) \setminus C$ that have both a neighbour and a non-neighbour in $C$, then $|D| + |V(G) \setminus C| \geqslant 2k$
nodes.label: thm:seagulls

nodes.name: Norin-Seymour seagull packing
nodes.statement: For example, \citet{NS26a} showed that for any integer $k\geqslant 1$, if a graph $G$ has $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \geqslant 3k$ and $\omega(G) \leqslant k$, then $G$ has $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint seagulls.

nodes.name: Chudnovsky-Seymour large clique seagull result
nodes.statement: As another example \citep{CS12}, for $t := \ceil{|V(G)| / 2}$, if $G$ is $t$-connected and the largest clique $Z$ in $G$ satisfies $\frac{3}{2} \left \lceil \frac{|V(G)|}{2} \right \rceil - \frac{|V(G)|}{2} \leqslant |Z| \leqslant t$, then there are $t-|Z|$ pairwise vertex-disjoint seagulls in $V(G) \setminus Z$, and consequently $G$ has a $K_t$ minor, and $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_half}.
assumptions: the largest clique $Z$ in $G$ satisfies $\frac{3}{2} \left \lceil \frac{|V(G)|}{2} \right \rceil - \frac{|V(G)|}{2} \leqslant |Z| \leqslant t$
conclusions: there are $t-|Z|$ pairwise vertex-disjoint seagulls in $V(G) \setminus Z$

nodes.name: Chudnovsky-Seymour clique-number criterion
nodes.statement: Every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and \begin{equation*} \omega(G) \geqslant \begin{cases} \left\lceil\frac{|V(G)|}{4}\right\rceil & \text{if $|V(G)|$ is even,} \\ \noalign{\vskip1pt} \left\lceil\frac{|V(G)|+3}{4}\right\rceil & \text{if $|V(G)|$ is odd,} \end{cases} \end{equation*} has $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/2$, and consequently $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_half}.
nodes.statement_short: If $\alpha(G)=2$ and $\omega(G)$ is at least about $|V(G)|/4$, then $\mathrm{had}(G)\ge|V(G)|/2$.
nodes.label: thm:seagullsN/4

nodes.name: Misreadings of Theorem 2.21
nodes.statement: \cref{thm:seagullsN/4} has been misunderstood by several authors (\citep[Theorem 1.6]{Bosse19}, \citep[Lemma 2]{Carter22}, \citep[Theorem 2.2]{Zhou23}). They wrongly conclude that $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi} instead of \nameref{conj:hc_half}. This is not implied.

nodes.name: inflated clique ratio
nodes.statement: Define the \defn{inflated clique ratio} of a non-empty graph $G$ as: \begin{equation*} \mathdefn{\mathrm{icr}(G)} = \inf \left \{\frac{\omega(G')}{|V(G')|} : \text{$G'$ is an inflation of $G$ with $|V(G')| > 0$}\right \}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{icr}(G)$ is the infimum of clique ratios over all non-empty inflations of $G$.

nodes.name: Basic bounds on icr
nodes.statement: For every non-empty graph $G$, $0 \leqslant \mathrm{icr}(G) \leqslant \omega(G) / |V(G)| \leqslant 1$, so $\mathrm{icr}(G)$ is finite and non-negative.

nodes.name: b-fold colouring
nodes.statement: For an integer $b \geqslant 1$, a \defn{$b$-fold colouring} of a graph $G$ is an assignment of sets of size $b$ to each vertex of $G$ such that adjacent vertices are assigned disjoint sets.

nodes.name: (a:b)-colouring
nodes.statement: For an integer $a \geqslant b$, an \defn{$(a:b)$-colouring} is a $b$-fold colouring using at most $a$ colours in total.

nodes.name: b-fold chromatic number
nodes.statement: The \defn{$b$-fold chromatic number}, denoted \defn{$\chi_b(G)$}, is the least integer $a$ such that an $(a:b)$-colouring exists.

nodes.name: fractional chromatic number
nodes.statement: The \defn{fractional chromatic number} of $G$ is defined as: \begin{equation*} \mathdefn{\chi_f(G)}:= \lim_{b \to \infty} \frac{\chi_b(G)}{b} = \inf_b \frac{\chi_b(G)}{b}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: fractional clique covering number
nodes.statement: The \defn{fractional clique covering number} of $G$, denoted $\mathdefn{\theta_f(G)}$, is defined to be $\chi_f(\overline{G})$.

nodes.name: clique cover
nodes.statement: A \defn{clique cover} of $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into a collection of cliques.

nodes.name: clique covering number
nodes.statement: The minimum number of cliques needed to cover $G$ is known as the \defn{clique covering number} of $G$, denoted $\mathdefn{\theta(G)}$.

nodes.name: Standard fractional colouring inequalities
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$, \begin{enumerate} \item $\omega(\overline{G}) \leqslant \theta_f(G) = \chi_f(\overline{G}) \leqslant \chi(\overline{G})$, \item $\theta_f(G) \leqslant \theta(G)$, and \item $\chi_f(\overline{G}) \alpha(\overline{G}) \geqslant |V(\overline{G})|$, and $\theta_f(G) \omega(G) \geqslant |V(G)|$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: obs:fractional

nodes.name: $\mathbb{Q}_{\geqslant 1}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{\mathbb{Q}_{\geqslant 1}}:=\{q \in \mathbb{Q}: q \geqslant 1\}$.

nodes.name: Clique multiset characterisation of fractional clique covering number
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \mathbb{Q}_{\geqslant 1}$ and let $G$ be a graph. Then $\theta_f(G) \leqslant k$ if and only if there are (not necessarily distinct) cliques $X_1, \dots, X_r$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ belongs to at least $r/k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$.
conclusions: $\theta_f(G) \leqslant k$ if and only if there are (not necessarily distinct) cliques $X_1, \dots, X_r$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ belongs to at least $r/k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$
equivalent_conditions: there are (not necessarily distinct) cliques $X_1, \dots, X_r$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ belongs to at least $r/k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$
nodes.label: lem:equiv_frac

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.23
nodes.statement: ($\Rightarrow$): Suppose $k = a/b$, where $a, b \geqslant 1$ are coprime integers. Suppose $\theta_f(G) = \chi_f(\overline{G}) = r/d$, where $r,d \geqslant 1$ are coprime integers, and $r \geqslant d$. For each vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $S_v$ be the set of $d$ colours assigned to $v$ out of the colours $\{1, \dots, r\}$ in the $(r:d)$-colouring of $\overline{G}$. For each $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$, let $X_i:= \{v \in V(G) : i \in S_v\}$. Since adjacent vertices in $\overline{G}$ receive disjoint sets, each $X_i$ is an independent set in $\overline{G}$ and hence a clique in $G$. Since $|S_v| = d$, each vertex is in exactly $d$ of the cliques $X_1, \dots, X_r$. By assumption, $\theta_f(G) = r/d \leqslant a/b = k$, so $rb \leqslant ad$ and $d \geqslant br/a = r/k$, implying that each vertex $v$ is in at least $r/k$ cliques, as desired. ($\Leftarrow$): Let $X_1, \dots, X_r$ be cliques such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ is in at least $r/k$ cliques. Suppose $k = a/b$, where $a, b \geqslant 1$ are coprime integers. For each $j \in \{1, \dots, r\}$, create $a$ copies of $X_j$ by defining, for each $i \in \{1, \dots, a\}$, $X_j^{(i)}:= X_j$. Then $\mathcal{X}:= (X_1^{(1)}, \dots, X_1^{(a)}, \dots, X_r^{(1)}, \dots, X_r^{(a)})$ is a multiset of $ra$ cliques, where each vertex $v \in V(G)$ is in at least $ra/k = rb$ cliques in $\mathcal{X}$. Assign each clique in $\mathcal{X}$ a distinct colour from $\{1, \dots, ra\}$, and for each vertex $v \in V(G)$, assign $v$ a set $S'_v$ of colours such that the colour $c \in \{1, \dots, ra\}$ is in $S'_v$ if and only if $v$ is contained in the clique of $\mathcal{X}$ coloured $c$. Observe that $|S'_v| \geqslant rb$. For distinct vertices $v_1, v_2 \in V(G)$, if $S_{v_1}' \cap S_{v_2}' \neq \varnothing$, then $v_1,v_2 \in X_i$ for some $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$, and $v_1v_2 \notin E(\overline{G})$. In $\overline{G}$, this defines a colouring using $ra$ colours where adjacent vertices receive disjoint sets. For each $v \in V(G)$, choose a subset $S_v \subseteq S'_v$ such that $|S_v| = rb$. This defines a $(ra: rb)$-colouring of $\overline{G}$, so $\theta_f(G) \leqslant ra/rb = k$.
nodes.statement_short: Colour classes of an $(r:d)$-colouring of the complement give cliques; conversely replicate cliques to build an $(ra:rb)$-colouring.

nodes.name: Proper inflations preserve fractional clique covering number
nodes.statement: Any proper inflation $G'$ of a graph $G$ satisfies $\theta_f(G) = \theta_f(G')$.
nodes.label: lem:inflation_frac

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.24
nodes.statement: $\theta_f(G') \leqslant \theta_f(G)$: Set $k:=\theta_f(G)$. \cref{lem:equiv_frac} implies that there are cliques $X_1, \dots, X_{r}$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ is in at least $r/k$ cliques of $X_1, \dots, X_{r}$. For each $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$, define $ X_i':= \bigcup_{v \in X_i} V(C_v)$, where $C_v$ is the clique in $G'$ that replaces $v$. Each vertex of $G'$ is contained in at least $r/k$ of $X_1', \dots, X_r'$. \cref{lem:equiv_frac} implies that $\theta_f(G') \leqslant k$. $\theta_f(G) \leqslant \theta_f(G')$: Set $k:=\theta_f(G')$. \cref{lem:equiv_frac} implies that there are cliques $X_1', \dots, X_r'$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G')$ is in at least $r/k$ of $X_1', \dots, X_r'$. Since $G'$ is a proper inflation of $G$, the projection map $p: V(G') \to V(G)$ is surjective, and projects cliques of $G'$ onto (not necessarily distinct) cliques of $G$. For each $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$, let $X_i:= p(X_i')$ be the projected clique in $G$. Since $p$ is surjective, for each vertex $v \in V(G)$, there is a vertex $v' \in V(G')$ such that $p(v') = v$. By assumption, $v'$ is in at least $r/k$ of $X_1', \dots, X_r'$. This implies that $v$ is in at least $r/k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$. \cref{lem:equiv_frac} implies $\theta_f(G) \leqslant k$.
nodes.statement_short: Both inequalities via Lemma 2.23: lift cliques to the inflation, and project cliques back using surjectivity.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.25
nodes.statement: Since $\theta_f(G)$ does not increase under taking induced subgraphs, the following is an immediate consequence of \cref{lem:inflation_frac}.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $\theta_f$ under induced subgraphs plus Lemma 2.24.

nodes.name: Inflations do not increase fractional clique covering number
nodes.statement: Any inflation $G'$ of a graph $G$ satisfies $\theta_f(G') \leqslant \theta_f(G)$.
nodes.label: cor:inflation_frac

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.26
nodes.statement: \cref{lem:jofre_lemma} follows from \cref{obs:fractional,lem:equiv_frac}.
nodes.statement_short: Follows from Observation 2.22 and Lemma 2.23.

nodes.name: Clique multiset bound on clique ratio
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, \dots, X_r$ be cliques of a graph $G$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ appears in at least $k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$. Then $\omega(G)/ |V(G)| \geqslant k/r$.
assumptions: $X_1, \dots, X_r$ be cliques of a graph $G$ such that each vertex $v \in V(G)$ appears in at least $k$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$
nodes.label: lem:jofre_lemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.27
nodes.statement: \cref{cor:inflation_frac}, \cref{lem:jofre_lemma}, and the definition of $\mathrm{icr}(G)$ imply that:
nodes.statement_short: Combine Corollary 2.25, Lemma 2.26 and the definition of icr.

nodes.name: Lower bound on icr by fractional clique covering
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$, \begin{equation*} \mathrm{icr}(G) \geqslant \frac{1}{\theta_f(G)} \geqslant \frac{1}{\theta(G)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:clique_cover

nodes.name: icr is at most 1/alpha
nodes.statement: For upper bounds on $\mathrm{icr}(G)$, note that for every graph $G$, $\mathrm{icr}(G) \leqslant 1/\alpha(G)$.

nodes.name: Proof that icr <= 1/alpha
nodes.statement: To see this, let $I \subseteq V(G)$ be a maximum independent set, and let $G' := G[I]$. Then $G'$ has no edges, so $\omega(G') = 1$, but $|V(G')| = \alpha(G)$. Therefore, $\mathrm{icr}(G) \leqslant 1/\alpha(G)$.
nodes.statement_short: Inflate a maximum independent set (other vertices size 0).

nodes.name: icr equals 1/alpha for perfect graphs
nodes.statement: For perfect graphs, equality holds.

nodes.name: Proof that icr = 1/alpha for perfect graphs
nodes.statement: If $G$ is perfect, then by the Weak Perfect Graph Theorem \citep[Proposition~5.5.3]{Diestel05}, $\overline{G}$ is perfect, so $\theta(G) = \chi(\overline{G}) = \omega(\overline{G}) = \alpha(G)$. The result follows from \cref{lem:clique_cover}.
nodes.statement_short: Weak Perfect Graph Theorem gives $\theta(G)=\alpha(G)$; apply Lemma 2.27.

nodes.name: For which k do graphs with theta_f <= k satisfy C?
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{C} \in \{	ext{
ameref{conj:hc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}, 
ameref{conj:shc_half}, 
ameref{conj:cdm}}\}$. For which values of $k \in \mathbb{Q}_{\geqslant 1}$ does the following hold: Every graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $	heta_f(G) \leqslant k$ satisfies $\mathfrak{C}$.
nodes.label: q:fractional

nodes.name: theta_f < 3 forces alpha <= 2
nodes.statement: For a graph $G$ with $\theta_f(G) < 3$, by \cref{lem:equiv_frac}, there are cliques $X_1, \dots, X_r$ of $G$ such that each vertex of $G$ belongs to strictly more than $r/3$ of $X_1, \dots, X_r$. If $S \subseteq V(G)$ is an independent set of size $3$, then by the Pigeonhole Principle, at least two vertices in $S$ are in some clique $X_i$, contradicting $S$ being an independent set. Thus, every graph with $\theta_f(G) < 3$ has $\alpha(G) \leqslant 2$.

nodes.name: Blasiak's theorem
nodes.statement: Every graph $G$ with $\theta_f(G) < 3$ and $|V(G)|$ even satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}.
nodes.label: thm:bla

nodes.name: Blasiak's good/bad edge theorem
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)|$ even. Suppose there is a partition of $E(G)$ into `good' and `bad' edges such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)] \item any two good edges that do not share an endpoint are adjacent, and \item for any two bad edges $uv$ and $vw$ that share an endpoint, $uw \in E(G)$, and \item if $u$ and $v$ are adjacent-twins then $uv$ is bad, and \item subject to (3), the number of good edges is as large as possible. \end{enumerate} Then either: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $G$ has a dominating edge, or \item $\kappa(G) \leqslant |V(G)|/2$, or \item $\omega(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/2$, or \item $G$ has a perfect matching $M$ of good edges such that $M$ is connected (and hence $M$ is dominating). \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)|$ even
any two good edges that do not share an endpoint are adjacent
for any two bad edges $uv$ and $vw$ that share an endpoint, $uw \in E(G)$
if $u$ and $v$ are adjacent-twins then $uv$ is bad
subject to (3), the number of good edges is as large as possible
conclusions: $G$ has a perfect matching $M$ of good edges such that $M$ is connected (and hence $M$ is dominating)
nodes.label: thm:good_bad

nodes.name: Deduction of Blasiak's theorem from the good/bad edge theorem
nodes.statement:
We deduce \cref{thm:bla} from \cref{thm:good_bad}. Note that if (b), (c) or (d) occurs, then $G$ satisfies 
ameref{conj:shc_half}. If (a) occurs, then we deduce that $G$ satisfies 
ameref{conj:shc_half} by applying induction to $G - \{u, v\}$, where $uv$ is the dominating edge of $G$. \cref{thm:good_bad} implies \cref{thm:bla} because for every graph with $	heta_f(G) < 3$, there is a partition of $E(G)$ into good and bad edges. To see this, observe that by \cref{lem:equiv_frac}, there is a multiset $\mathcal{X}:=(X_1, \dots, X_r)$ in $G$ such that each vertex of $G$ is in strictly more than $r/3$ cliques of $\mathcal{X}$. Partition $E(G)$ as follows. For an edge $uv \in E(G)$, let $\mathdefn{n(uv)}$ be the size of the multiset $\mathdefn{N(uv)}:= (X_i \in \mathcal{X}: 	ext{$u$ or $v$ is in $X_i$})$. An edge $uv$ is good if $n(uv) > r/2$, and bad otherwise. If $uv$ and $xy$ are good edges not sharing an endpoint, then since $n(uv), n(xy) > r/2$, we have $N(uv) \cap N(xy) 
eq \varnothing$, so there is a clique in $\mathcal{X}$ containing an endpoint of $uv$ and an endpoint of $xy$. Thus, two good edges that do not share an endpoint are adjacent. If $uv$ and $vw$ are bad, then $n(uv) \leqslant r/2$ and $n(vw) \leqslant r/2$. However, since there are strictly more than $r/3$ cliques containing $u$, there are strictly less than $r/6$ cliques of $\mathcal{X}$ containing $v$ but not $u$. Similarly, there are strictly less than $r/6$ cliques of $\mathcal{X}$ containing $v$ but not $w$. However, since $v$ is in strictly more than $r/3$ cliques of $\mathcal{X}$, there is a clique in $\mathcal{X}$ containing $u,v$ and $w$. Thus, $uw \in E(G)$.
nodes.statement_short: Outcomes (b)-(d) give SHC$_{n/2}$, (a) by induction; build the good/bad partition from a clique multiset of Lemma 2.23.

nodes.name: Good/bad partitions need not exist
nodes.statement: It is tempting to conjecture that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has a partition of $E(G)$ into good and bad edges satisfying the assumptions in \cref{thm:good_bad}. However, \citet{Blasiak07} demonstrated that this is false.

nodes.name: Blasiak's conjecture for theta_f < 3
nodes.statement: Every graph $G$ with $\theta_f(G) < 3$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}.
nodes.label: conj:bla

nodes.name: Carter: HC holds for alpha=2 graphs on at most 30 vertices
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \leqslant 30$. Then $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}. Therefore, any minimal counterexample to \nameref{conj:hc_chi} has at least $31$ vertices, and $|V(G)|$ is odd.
conclusions: any minimal counterexample to \nameref{conj:hc_chi} has at least $31$ vertices, and $|V(G)|$ is odd
nodes.label: thm:carter30

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.30
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. By \cref{thm:equiv}, $G$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_half}. Since $K_8$ is 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}-unavoidable~\citep{Carter22}, $\omega(G) \geqslant 8$. If $|V(G)| \leqslant 30$, then the assumptions of \cref{thm:seagullsN/4} are satisfied, so $G$ satisfies 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, a contradiction. Therefore, $|V(G)| \geqslant 31$. By Property 	extup{(ef{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})} of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}, $|V(G)|$ is odd.
nodes.statement_short: A minimal counterexample has $\omega\ge 8$ ($K_8$ unavoidable), so Theorem 2.21 applies when $|V(G)|\le 30$.

nodes.name: Inflated clique ratio above 1/4 + 1/62 implies HC for inflations
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $\mathrm{icr}(G) \geqslant \frac{1}{4} + \varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon:=1/62$. Then any inflation of $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
assumptions: $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $\mathrm{icr}(G) \geqslant \frac{1}{4}  + \varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon:=1/62$
nodes.label: thm:icr1/4

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.31
nodes.statement:
Let $G'$ be an inflation of $G$ that fails 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. Let $H$ be a minimal induced subgraph of $G'$ that is a counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. Note that $H$ is also an inflation of $G$, and $H$ is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:hc_chi}. By \cref{thm:carter30}, $|V(H)| \geqslant 31$ and $|V(H)|$ is odd. By \cref{thm:equiv}, $H$ fails 
ameref{conj:hc_half}. Since $\mathrm{icr}(G) \geqslant  rac{1}{4} + \varepsilon$, $ \omega(H) \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{|V(H)|}{4} +  rac{|V(H)|}{62}ight ceil \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{|V(H)| + 2}{4} ightceil$. If $|V(H)| \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $|V(H)| = 4k + 1$ for some integer $k$. Then $ \omega(H) \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{(4k+1)+ 2}{4} ightceil = k + 1$. By \cref{thm:seagullsN/4}, since $\omega(H) \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{|V(H)| + 3}{4} ightceil = k + 1$, $H$ satisfies 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, a contradiction. If $|V(H)| = 4k + 3$ for some integer $k$, then $ \omega(H) \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{(4k + 3) + 2}{4} ightceil = k + 2$. By \cref{thm:seagullsN/4}, since $\omega(H) \geqslant \left\lceil  rac{|V(H)| + 3}{4} ightceil = k + 2$, $H$ satisfies 
ameref{conj:hc_half}, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: A minimal counterexample inflation has $\ge 31$ odd vertices; the icr bound makes its clique large enough for Theorem 2.21 in both residues mod 4.

nodes.name: theta_f <= 124/33 implies HC for inflations
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $\theta_f(G) \leqslant 124/33 \approx 3.7575\dots$. Then any inflation of $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
nodes.label: thm:124/33

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.32
nodes.statement: By \cref{lem:clique_cover}, $\mathrm{icr}(G) \geqslant \frac{33}{124} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{62}$. The result follows from \cref{thm:icr1/4}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.27 gives icr$\ge 33/124$; apply Theorem 2.31.

nodes.name: Why the constant 124/33 cannot be pushed to 4
nodes.statement: In some sense, \cref{thm:seagullsN/4} should allow us to push the constant $124/33$ in \cref{thm:124/33} up to $4$. After all, every graph with $\theta_f(G) \leqslant 4$ has $\omega(G)/|V(G)| \geqslant 1/4$, and \cref{thm:seagullsN/4} says that \nameref{conj:hc_half} holds for graphs with $\omega(G) / |V(G)|$ slightly larger than $1/4$. We are unable to push the constant $124/33$ up to $4$ because of the $\varepsilon$ term in \cref{thm:icr1/4}, which depends on the lower bound on the size of a minimum counterexample established in \cref{thm:carter30}.

nodes.name: Clique collections lift to proper inflations
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{K}$ be a collection of cliques of $G$ whose union covers $V(G)$. Then any proper inflation $G'$ of $G$ has a collection of cliques $\mathcal{K}'$ whose union covers $V(G')$ such that $|\mathcal{K}| = |\mathcal{K}'|$ and $\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K'}} |Q| = |V(G')| - |V(G)| + \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K}} |Q|$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{K}$ be a collection of cliques of $G$ whose union covers $V(G)$
conclusions: any proper inflation $G'$ of $G$ has a collection of cliques $\mathcal{K}'$ whose union covers $V(G')$ such that $|\mathcal{K}| = |\mathcal{K}'|$ and $\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K'}} |Q| = |V(G')| - |V(G)| + \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K}} |Q|$
nodes.label: lem:cc2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.33
nodes.statement: Let $G'$ be a proper inflation of $G$. We induct on $|V(G')|$. Let $V(G) = \{ v_1, \dots, v_n \}$. The base case when $|V(G')| = |V(G)|$ is straightforward by taking $\mathcal{K}' = \mathcal{K}$. For the induction step, suppose $G'$ is an inflation of $G$ with inflation sizes $k_1, \dots, k_n$, with $k_i \geqslant 1$ for each $i \in \{ 1, \dots, n \}$. Since $|V(G')| > |V(G)|$, there is an index $i$ such that $k_i \geqslant 2$. Let $G''$ be an inflation of $G$ with inflation sizes $k_1, \dots k_{i-1}, k_i - 1, k_{i+1} \dots,k_n$. Then $G''$ is a proper inflation of $G$. By induction hypothesis, there is a collection of cliques $\mathcal{K}''$ of $G''$ whose union covers $V(G'')$ such that $\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K''}} |Q| = |V(G'')| - |V(G)| + \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{K}} |Q|$. Note that $G'$ is an inflation of $G''$ obtained from replacing a vertex $w$ with a clique of size $2$. Since the union of $\mathcal{K}''$ covers $V(G'')$, there is a clique $K'' \in \mathcal{K}''$ such that $w \in K''$. Let $v \in V(G') \setminus V(G'')$, and note that $v$ and $w$ are adjacent-twins. Let $K':= K'' \cup \{ v \}$. $K'$ is a clique in $G'$ since $v$ and $w$ are adjacent-twins, so $v$ is adjacent to each vertex in $K''$ in $G'$. Then $\mathcal{K}':= \mathcal{K}'' \cup \{ K' \} \setminus \{ K'' \} $ is a collection of cliques of $G'$ satisfying the desired properties.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $|V(G')|$: add one adjacent-twin to the clique containing its twin.

nodes.name: Four-clique-cover criterion for HC_{n/2} of inflations
nodes.statement: If a graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has four cliques $(Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, Q_4)$ whose union covers $V(G)$ with $\sum_{i=1}^4 |Q_i| \geqslant |V(G)| + 2$, then any proper inflation of $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_half}.
assumptions: a graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has four cliques $(Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, Q_4)$ whose union covers $V(G)$ with $\sum_{i=1}^4 |Q_i| \geqslant |V(G)| + 2$
nodes.label: thm:fcc

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.34
nodes.statement: Let $G'$ be a proper inflation of $G$. By \cref{lem:cc2}, there are cliques of $G'$ $(Q_1', Q_2', Q_3', Q_4')$ whose union covers $V(G')$ such that \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=1}^4 |Q_i'| = |V(G')| - |V(G)| + \sum_{i=1}^4 |Q_i| \geqslant |V(G')| + 2. \end{equation*} Therefore, \begin{equation*} 4\omega(G') \geqslant \sum_{i=1}^4 |Q_i'| \geqslant |V(G')| + 2, \end{equation*} implying $\omega(G') \geqslant \left\lceil \frac{|V(G')| + 2}{4}\right\rceil$, and \cref{thm:seagullsN/4} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: Lift the four cliques by Lemma 2.33, so $\omega(G')\ge\lceil(|V(G')|+2)/4\rceil$; apply Theorem 2.21.

nodes.name: connected matching number and had_2
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{\mathrm{cm}(G)}$ be the largest size of a connected matching in $G$, and recall that $\mathdefn{\mathrm{had}_2(G)}$ is the order of the largest clique model in $G$ such that each branch set has one or two vertices.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: cm(G) <= had_2(G)
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to see that $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Furedi-Gyarfas-Simonyi small cases of 4-CM
nodes.statement: For each $t \in \{1, \dots, 17\}$, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \geqslant 4t - 1$ has a connected matching of size $t$. Therefore, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \leqslant 67$ satisfies \nameref{conj:4-CM}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture
conclusions: has a connected matching of size $t$
nodes.label: thm:t=16

nodes.name: Chen et al.: 4-CM for t <= 22
nodes.statement: The bound was later improved to $t \in \{1, \dots, 22\}$ by \citet{chen2025connected}. Therefore, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \leqslant 87$ satisfies \nameref{conj:4-CM}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Cambie's clique bound
nodes.statement: For any integer $t \geqslant 1$, if $G$ is a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $|V(G)| = 4t - 1$ and $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t - 1$, then $\omega(G) \leqslant \mathrm{cm}(G)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $|V(G)| = 4t - 1$ and $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t - 1$
nodes.label: lem:cambie1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.36
nodes.statement: If $G$ is disconnected, then $G$ is the union of two complete graphs. One component of $G$ has order at least $2t$, implying $\mathrm{cm}(G) \geqslant t$. Hence $G$ is connected. Note that $\mathrm{cm}(G) \geqslant \floor{\omega(G) /2}$, so $\omega(G) \leqslant 2t-1$. By \cref{obs:non-neighbours}, $\delta(G) \geqslant |V(G)|-1 - \omega(G)\geqslant 2t-1$. Let $A$ be a clique of order $\omega(G)$ and let $B=V(G) \setminus A.$ Let $M$ be the largest matching in the bipartite subgraph induced by the edges between $A$ and $B$. Any matching from $A$ to $B$ is connected since $A$ is a clique, so $\left|M\right| \leqslant \mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t-1$. Suppose for contradiction that $\omega(G) > \mathrm{cm}(G) \geqslant |M|$. This implies there is a vertex $x \in A$ unmatched by $M$. However, there is no neighbour of $x$ contained in $B - V(M)$, otherwise this contradicts the maximality of $M$. Therefore, all neighbours of $x$ are contained in $A \cup V(M)$. Since $\deg_G(x) \geqslant 2t - 1$, $|A \cup V(M)| \geqslant 2t$. Observe that $2|M| + |A \setminus V(M)| = |V(M) \cup (A \setminus V(M))| = |A \cup V(M)| = |A| + |M| \geqslant 2t$. Therefore, $|A \setminus V(M)| \geqslant 2t - 2|M|$, implying there are at least $2t - 2|M|$ vertices in $A$ left unmatched by $M$. We can extend the matching $M$ by pairing the remaining unmatched vertices of $A$, obtaining a connected matching of size $t$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Match a maximum clique to the rest; an unmatched clique vertex has high degree, so the matching extends to size $t$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Cambie's had_2 bound
nodes.statement: For every integer $t \geqslant 1$, if $G$ is a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $|V(G)| = 4t - 1$, and $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t - 1$, then $\mathrm{had}_2(G) \leqslant \mathrm{cm}(G)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$, $|V(G)| = 4t - 1$, and $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t - 1$
nodes.label: lem:cambie2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.37
nodes.statement: Choose a $K_{\mathrm{had}_2(G)}$-model $\mathcal{M}$ of $G$ with $k_1$ singletons and $k_2$ edges so that $k_2$ is maximised. Thus, $k_1 + k_2 = \mathrm{had}_2(G)$. Since $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t-1$, $k_2 \leqslant t- 1$. Suppose to the contrary that $\left|\mathcal{M}\right| = k_1 + k_2 > \mathrm{cm}(G)$. Then $k_1 \geqslant 1$, and let $x$ be one of the $k_1$ singletons in $\mathcal{M}$. \cref{lem:cambie1} asserts that $\omega(G) \leqslant \mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t -1$, so by \cref{obs:non-neighbours} $ \delta(G) \geqslant |V(G)|-1 - \omega(G)\geqslant 3t-1$. However, the collection $\mathcal{M}$ contains at most $k_1+2k_2\leqslant 3(t-1) = 3t - 3$ vertices, implying that $x$ has a neighbour outside $\mathcal{M}$. Pairing $x$ with this neighbour contradicts the maximality of $k_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a $K_{\mathrm{had}_2}$-model maximising edge branch sets; a singleton has an outside neighbour by Lemma 2.36, contradicting maximality.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Cambie: HC_{n/2} implies 4-CM
nodes.statement: \nameref{conj:hc_half} implies \nameref{conj:4-CM}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture
nodes.label: thm:cambie

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.38
nodes.statement:
We show the contrapositive. Suppose 
ameref{conj:4-CM} is false and 
ameref{conj:hc_half} holds. Let $G$ be a graph with $4t - 1$ vertices with $\mathrm{cm}(G) \leqslant t- 1$. Since 
ameref{conj:hc_half} holds, there is a $K_{2t}$-model of $G$. For each $i \geqslant 1$, let $k_i$ be the number of branch sets of size $i$, and let $k:= \sum_{i \geqslant 3} k_i$. \cref{lem:cambie2} implies $k_1 + k_2 \leqslant \mathrm{had}_2(G) \leqslant t-1$. However, $k_1 + k_2 + k = 2t$ and $k_1 + 2k_2 + 3k \leqslant 4t - 1$. Thus, $ 6t = 3(k_1+k_2+k) \leqslant k_1+2k_2+3k + 2(k_1+k_2) \leqslant 4t-1 +2(t-1)=6t-3$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Contrapositive: count branch-set sizes of a $K_{2t}$-model against Lemma 2.37.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: connected matching function f
nodes.statement: Let $\mathdefn{f}: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a function such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ and $|V(G)| \geqslant t$ has a connected matching of size at least $f(t)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Kim's Ramsey bound R(3,k)
nodes.statement: The asymptotic magnitude of the Ramsey number $R(3,k)$ was determined by \citet{Kim95}, who proved that a $t$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ has $\omega(G) \in \Omega(\sqrt{t \log t})$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: f(t) is Omega(sqrt(t log t))
nodes.statement: Since the complete graph on $2t$ vertices contains a connected matching of size $t$, $f(t) \in \Omega(\sqrt{t \log t})$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Furedi-Gyarfas-Simonyi bound on f
nodes.statement: \citet{furedi2005connected} showed $f(t) \in \Omega(t^{2/3})$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Blasiak bound on f
nodes.statement: Later, \citet{Blasiak07} showed $f(t) \in \Omega(t^{4/5})$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Fox bound on f
nodes.statement: \citet{Fox10} currently holds the record, proving $f(t) \in \Omega(t^{4/5} \log^{1/5}t)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Connected Matchings and Weakenings of Hadwiger's Conjecture

nodes.name: Norin-Seymour dense minor theorem
nodes.statement: \citet{NS26a} proved that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$ contains a minor $H$ with $|V(H)| = \ceil{|V(G)|/ 2}$ and $ |E(H)| \geqslant (\gamma - o(1)) \binom{|V(H)|}{2}$, where $\gamma \approx 0.986882$.
conclusions: contains a minor $H$ with $|V(H)| = \ceil{|V(G)|/ 2}$ and  $ |E(H)| \geqslant (\gamma - o(1)) \binom{|V(H)|}{2}$

nodes.name: Dense variant of Linear-CM
nodes.statement: Using ideas from \citep{NS26a}, \citet{yip2025dense} proved a dense variant of \nameref{conj:linear_cm}: for any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $c := c(\varepsilon)$ such that for every integer $t \geqslant 1$, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) \leqslant 2$ and $|V(G)| \geqslant ct$ contains a matching $M$ with $|M| = t$ such that the density of adjacent edge pairs is at least $1 - \varepsilon$.
conclusions: contains a matching $M$ with $|M| = t$ such that the density of adjacent edge pairs is at least $1 - \varepsilon$

nodes.name: claw-free
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is \defn{claw-free} if it is $K_{1,3}$-free (that is, no vertex has three pairwise non-adjacent neighbours).

nodes.name: CDM fails for claw-free graphs
nodes.statement: Although every graph with $\alpha(G) = 2$ is claw-free, \nameref{conj:cdm} is false for the larger class of claw-free graphs (e.g., $C_7$).

nodes.name: Chudnovsky-Fradkin linear Hadwiger for claw-free graphs
nodes.statement: For claw-free graphs, \citet{chudnovsky_approximate_2010} proved a linear version of Hadwiger's Conjecture: every claw-free graph $G$ with no $K_{t+1}$-minor is $\floor{3t/2}$-colourable.

nodes.name: Fradkin's theorem for claw-free graphs
nodes.statement: Every connected claw-free graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) \geqslant 3$ satisfies $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant |V(G)|/\alpha(G)$.
also_stated_at: For claw-free graphs, \citet{FradkinClique12} proved that the only exceptions to \cref{conj:indep} are graphs with $\alpha(G) = 2$.

nodes.name: quasi-line graph
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is \defn{quasi-line} if the neighbourhood of each vertex is the union of two cliques.
differentia: the neighbourhood of each vertex is the union of two cliques

nodes.name: Reed-Seymour: HC for line graphs
nodes.statement: \citet{reed_hadwigers_2004} first proved Hadwiger’s Conjecture for line graphs of multigraphs.
conclusions: Hadwiger’s Conjecture for line graphs of multigraphs

nodes.name: Chudnovsky-Ovetsky: HC for quasi-line graphs
nodes.statement: This was later extended to quasi-line graphs by \citet{CO08}, who proved $\mathrm{had}(G) \geqslant \chi(G)$ for any quasi-line graph $G$.

nodes.name: Inflations of quasi-line graphs are quasi-line
nodes.statement: Observe that any inflation of a quasi-line graph is a quasi-line graph.
assumptions: any inflation of a quasi-line graph

nodes.name: PST: SHC_{n/2} for inflations of graphs on at most 11 vertices
nodes.statement: \citet{PST03} proved \nameref{conj:shc_half} for inflations of small graphs: any inflation of $G$ with $|V(G)| \leqslant 11$ and $\alpha(G) = 2$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}.

nodes.name: Andrasfai graph
nodes.statement: For $d \geqslant 1$, the \defn{Andr\'asfai graph with parameter $d$}, denoted \defn{$\Gamma_d$}, is the $d$-regular triangle-free diameter-$2$ graph with $V(\Gamma_d) = \{v_1, \dots, v_{3d-1}\}$, and two vertices $v_i$ and $v_j$ are adjacent if and only if $|i - j| \equiv 1 \pmod{3}$.

nodes.name: PST: CDM for inflations of Andrasfai graphs
nodes.statement: \citet{PST03} proved \nameref{conj:cdm}\footnotemark\footnotetext{They actually showed that any inflation of $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}. However, their proof can be modified to establish this.} for inflations of Andr\'asfai graphs, which includes the $5$-cycle.

nodes.name: Pedersen-Toft: HC for inflations of odd anticycles
nodes.statement: Lastly, \citet{PPT16} showed that for each $p \geqslant 1$, if $G$ is an inflation of $\overline{C_{2p+1}}$, then $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
also_stated_at: \citet{PPT16} showed that for each $p \geqslant 1$, if $G$ is an inflation of $\overline{C_{2p+1}}$, then $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.

nodes.name: Hoffman-Singleton theorem
nodes.statement: Graphs with girth $5$ are triangle-free, and \citet{HS60} famously proved that there are finitely many graphs with diameter $2$ and girth $5$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$
conclusions: there are finitely many graphs with diameter $2$ and girth $5$

nodes.name: Existence of the 57-regular Moore graph
nodes.statement: Any other diameter-$2$ girth-$5$ graph is $57$-regular with $3250$ vertices, and it is open if such a graph exists.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$

nodes.name: CDM for inflations of complements of girth-5 graphs
nodes.statement: Any inflation of the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$
also_stated_at: Any inflation of the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}
assumptions: Any inflation of the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$
nodes.label: thm:girth_5

nodes.name: Why inflations are the main point of Theorem 3.40
nodes.statement:
Graphs with girth at least $5$ are $C_4$-free, so their complements are $\overline{C_4}$-free, and therefore they satisfy 
ameref{conj:cdm}, since every graph $H$ with $|V(H)| \leqslant 4$ and $\alpha(H) \leqslant 2$ is 
ameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable (see \cref{ss:induced}). Therefore, the main claim of \cref{thm:girth_5} is that 
ameref{conj:cdm} continues to hold for their inflations, which may contain $\overline{C_4}$ as a subgraph.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.40
nodes.statement: We may assume that $G$ is a connected inflation of a graph $H$, where $\overline{H}$ has girth at least $5$. By definition, $G$ is obtained by replacing each vertex $x \in V(H)$ with a clique $C_x$. Let $H'$ be the subgraph of $H$ induced by the set $\{x \in V(H): |C_x| > 0\}$. Then $G$ is a proper inflation of $H'$. Since $G$ is connected, $H'$ is connected. If $H'$ is $C_5$-free, then because $\overline{C_5} \cong C_5$ and $C_5$ is adjacent-twin-free, by \cref{lem:blow_up_avoidant}, $G$ is $C_5$-free as well. Therefore, by \cref{thm:c5}, $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}. Therefore, we may assume $H'$ contains an induced $C_5$. Label its vertices $a,b,c,d,e$ clockwise. By \cref{obs:preserve}, $\alpha(H') = 2$, and thus the neighbourhood of each vertex $x \in V(H') \setminus \{a,b,c,d,e\}$ contains three consecutive vertices of $C_5$. Suppose for contradiction that $|N_{H'}(x) \cap \{a,b,c,d,e\}| = 3$ for some $x \in V(H') \setminus \{a,b,c,d,e\}$. Without loss of generality, $N_{H'}(x) \cap \{a,b,c,d,e\} = \{a,b,c\}$. Then $de, bx \in E(H')$ are non-adjacent edges in $H'$, so $dxeb$ is a $4$-cycle in $\overline{H'}$, which contradicts that the girth of $\overline{H'}$ is at least $5$. Therefore, every vertex $x \in V(H') \setminus \{a,b,c,d,e\}$ is adjacent to at least four vertices in $\{a,b,c,d,e\}$. Relabelling the vertices of $C_5$ anticlockwise and mirroring the vertices if needed, we may assume that $|C_a| = \min\{|C_a|, \dots, |C_e|\}$ and $|C_c| \leqslant |C_d|$. Let $M_1$ be a matching from $C_a$ to $C_e$ saturating $C_a$, and let $M_2$ be a matching from $C_c$ to $C_d$ saturating $C_c$. Since $G$ is a proper inflation of $H'$, $|M_1| = |C_a| \geqslant 1$ and $|M_2| = |C_c| \geqslant 1$, so $M_1 \cup M_2$ is a non-empty matching of $G$. For an edge $uv \in M_1$, since each vertex $x \in V(H') \setminus \{a,b,c,d,e\}$ is adjacent to at least four vertices in $\{a,b,c,d,e\}$, only vertices in $C_c$ are non-adjacent to $uv$. However, $M_2$ saturates $C_c$. Similarly, for an edge $uv \in M_2$, only vertices in $C_a$ are non-adjacent to $uv$, but $M_1$ saturates $C_a$. Thus, $M_1 \cup M_2$ is a non-empty connected dominating matching of $G$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a proper inflation containing an induced $C_5$; girth forces outside vertices to see 4 of its vertices, then match $C_a$-$C_e$ and $C_c$-$C_d$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$

nodes.name: CDM for inflations of complements of Moore graphs
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the complement of the $5$-cycle, or the complement of the Petersen graph, or the complement of the Hoffman-Singleton graph, or the complement of a hypothetical $57$-regular graph with girth $5$. Then any inflation of $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}.

nodes.label: thm:girth_5_eg

nodes.name: SHC for inflations of complements of girth-5 graphs
nodes.statement: Any inflation of the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_chi}.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$
assumptions: Any inflation of the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$
nodes.label: thm:girth_5_hc

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.42
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be an inflation of $H$ with $\alpha(G) = 2$, where $H$ is the complement of a graph with girth at least $5$. Suppose for contradiction that $G$ fails 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}. Let $G'$ be a minimal induced subgraph of $G$ such that $G'$ fails 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}. Then $G'$ is an inflation of $H$ and is a minimal counterexample to 
ameref{conj:shc_chi}. By \cref{thm:equiv}, $G'$ fails 
ameref{conj:shc_half}, implying that $G'$ is connected. By \cref{thm:girth_5}, $G'$ contains a non-empty connected dominating matching, a contradiction to Property 	extup{(ef{prop:no_connected_dominating_matching})} of \cref{thm:minimal_properties}.
nodes.statement_short: A minimal SHC counterexample inflation is connected and has a CDM by Theorem 3.40, contradicting Property (6).

nodes.name: SHC for inflations of anticycles
nodes.statement: For each $k \geqslant 3$, if $G$ is an inflation of $\overline{C_k}$, then $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_chi}.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$
nodes.label: cor:anticycles

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.43
nodes.statement: The case when $k = 3$ is straightforward. If $G$ is an inflation of $\overline{C_4}$, then $G$ is a disjoint union of two non-adjacent complete graphs, so $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_chi}. If $G$ is an inflation of $\overline{C_k}$ for $k \geqslant 5$, then by \cref{thm:girth_5_hc}, $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_chi}.
nodes.statement_short: Cases $k=3,4$ directly; $k\ge 5$ by Corollary 3.42.
nodes.section: 3.1 Complements of Graphs with Girth At Least $5$

nodes.name: Kneser graphs K(n,k) with 2k<=n<=3k-1 are triangle-free
nodes.statement: In particular, when $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k-1$, $K(n,k)$ is triangle-free, implying $\alpha(\overline{K(n,k)}) = 2$.

nodes.name: Diameter of K(3k-1,k)
nodes.statement: When $n = 3k - 1$, $\mathrm{diam}(K(n,k)) = 2$ (\citep{valencia2005diameter}, see Property \textup{(\ref{prop:complement_diameter_2})}).

nodes.name: Kneser graphs are Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: \citet{merino2023kneser} proved that for all values of $n$ and $k$, $K(n,k)$ is Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Complements of odd-order Kneser graphs are vertex-critical
nodes.statement: If $n$ and $k$ are chosen so that $|V(K(n,k))|$ is odd, then by taking alternate edges of a Hamiltonian cycle, for each vertex $v \in V(K(n,k))$, $K(n,k) - v$ has a perfect matching. By \cref{lem:chromatic_matching}, this implies that $\mu(K(n,k)) = (|V(K(n,k))| - 1) / 2$, so $|V(K(n,k))| = 2 \chi(\overline{K(n,k)}) - 1$ and $\overline{K(n,k)}$ is vertex-critical (see Properties \textup{(\ref{prop:vertex_critical})} and \textup{(\ref{prop:size_equals_2chi_minus_1})}).

nodes.name: Thomassen: complements of K(3k-1,k) are counterexamples to Hajos
nodes.statement: For sufficiently large $k$, \citet{Thomassen05} proved that $\overline{K(3k-1,k)}$ is a counterexample to Haj{\'o}s’ Conjecture.
conclusions: $\overline{K(3k-1,k)}$ is a counterexample to Haj{\'o}s’ Conjecture

nodes.name: Xu-Zhang: HC for complements of Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: Motivated by this comment, \citet{XZ17} proved that Hadwiger's Conjecture holds for all complements of Kneser graphs, including when $\alpha(\overline{K(n,k)}) = 2$.
conclusions: Hadwiger's Conjecture holds for all complements of Kneser graphs

nodes.name: Fractional chromatic number of Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: For integers $n,k \geqslant 1$ such that $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 1$, $\theta_f(\overline{K(n,k)}) = \chi_f(K(n,k)) = n/k$.
nodes.label: lem:frac_chromatic_kneser

nodes.name: SHC_{n/2} for even inflations of complements of Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: For integers $n,k \geqslant 1$ such that $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 1$, any inflation of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ with an even number of vertices satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}.
also_stated_at: For integers $n,k \geqslant 1$ such that $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 1$, any inflation of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ with an even number of vertices satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}
assumptions: any inflation of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ with an even number of vertices
nodes.label: lem:kneser_graphs

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.45
nodes.statement: By \cref{lem:frac_chromatic_kneser}, $\theta_f(\overline{K(n,k)}) = n/k < 3$. Applying \cref{thm:bla} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_f=n/k<3$ by Lemma 3.44, then Blasiak's Theorem 2.28.

nodes.name: HC for inflations of complements of triangle-free Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: For integers $n,k \geqslant 1$ such that $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 1$, any inflation of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
also_stated_at: For integers $n,k \geqslant 1$ such that $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 1$, any inflation of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}
nodes.label: lem:kneser_graphs2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.46
nodes.statement: By \cref{lem:frac_chromatic_kneser}, $\theta_f(\overline{K(n,k)}) = n/k < 3$. Applying \cref{thm:124/33} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_f=n/k<3$ by Lemma 3.44, then Theorem 2.32.

nodes.name: Dominating edges do not suffice for Kneser inflations
nodes.statement: Note that when $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 2$, $\overline{K(n,k)}$ has a dominating edge. However, this does not imply \cref{lem:kneser_graphs,lem:kneser_graphs2} for $2k \leqslant n \leqslant 3k - 2$, since there are induced subgraphs of $\overline{K(n,k)}$ with no dominating edge.

nodes.name: Generalised Kneser complements have alpha <= 2
nodes.statement: For integers $n, k, t \geqslant 1$ satisfying $2k - t \leqslant n < 3k - 3t + 3$, $\alpha(K(n, k, \geqslant t)) \leqslant 2$.
assumptions: integers $n, k, t \geqslant 1$ satisfying $2k - t \leqslant n < 3k - 3t + 3$

nodes.name: Inclusion-exclusion argument for alpha <= 2
nodes.statement: This is because if there are $k$-sets $S_1, S_2, S_3$ such that $|S_i \cap S_j| \leqslant t - 1$ for each distinct $i,j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, then by the inclusion-exclusion principle, \begin{equation*} |S_1 \cup S_2 \cup S_3| = |S_1| + |S_2| + |S_3| - |S_1 \cap S_2| - |S_1 \cap S_3| - |S_2 \cap S_3| + |S_1 \cap S_2 \cap S_3| \geqslant 3k - 3(t-1). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Three pairwise weakly-intersecting $k$-sets would need more than $n$ elements by inclusion-exclusion.

nodes.name: t-intersecting family
nodes.statement: A \defn{$t$-intersecting} family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ is a collection of subsets such that if $A, B \in \mathcal{F}$, then $\left|A \cap B\right| \geqslant t$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}$
nodes.statement: Define, for each $r$ such that $t + 2r \leqslant n$, \begin{equation*} \mathdefn{\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}} := \left\{ A \in \binom{[n]}{k}: \left|A \cap \{ 1, \dots, t+2r \}\right| \geqslant t+ r \right\}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: F_{n,k,t,r} is t-intersecting
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}$ is a $t$-intersecting family of sets, since if $S = \{1, \dots, t + 2r\}$, then for any $A_1, A_2 \in \mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}$, \begin{equation*} t + 2r \geqslant |(A_1 \cap S) \cup (A_2 \cap S)| = |A_1 \cap S| + |A_2 \cap S| - |A_1 \cap A_2 \cap S| \geqslant 2(t+r) - |A_1 \cap A_2 \cap S|. \end{equation*} Therefore, $|A_1 \cap A_2| \geqslant t$.

nodes.name: Size of F_{n,k,t,r}
nodes.statement: \left|\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}\right| = \sum_{i=t+r}^{t+2r} \binom{t+2r}{i} \binom{n - t - 2r}{k - i}. \tag{1}
nodes.label: eq:frac

nodes.name: Ahlswede-Khachatrian Complete Intersection Theorem
nodes.statement: The maximum size of a $t$-intersecting family in $\binom{[n]}{k}$ is at most $\max\limits_{r: t + 2r \leqslant n} \left|\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}\right|$.
also_stated_at: \citet{ahlswede1997complete} proved that the maximum size of a $t$-intersecting family is achieved by one of the $\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}$ families.
conclusions: The maximum size of a $t$-intersecting family in $\binom{[n]}{k}$ is at most $\max\limits_{r: t + 2r \leqslant n} \left|\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}\right|$
nodes.label: thm:akt

nodes.name: $f_{n,k,t}$
nodes.statement: Define: \begin{equation*} \mathdefn{f_{n,k,t}}:= \max_{r: t + 2r \leqslant n} \left|\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}\right|. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Clique number of K(n,k,>=t)
nodes.statement: By \cref{thm:akt}, $\omega(K(n,k,\geqslant t)) = f_{n,k,t}$.

nodes.name: Fractional clique covering number of generalised Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: For integers $n,k,t \geqslant 1$, $ \theta_f(K(n,k,\geqslant t)) = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{f_{n,k,t}} $.
nodes.label: thm:fractional_kneser_graphs

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.48
nodes.statement: Let $r \geqslant 0$ be an integer such that $t + 2r \leqslant n$ and $\left|\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}\right| = f_{n,k,t}$, and let $s := t + 2r$. Fix a subset $S$ of $[n]$ of size $s$. Define: \begin{equation*} \mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}^S := \left\{ A \in \binom{[n]}{k}: \left|A \cap S \right| \geqslant t+ r \right\}. \end{equation*} $\mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}^S $ is a $t$-intersecting family, and the corresponding vertices induce a complete graph in $K(n, k, \geqslant t)$. Let $\mathcal{K}:= \{ \mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}^S: S \in \binom{[n]}{s} \}$ be a collection of subsets of $\binom{[n]}{k}$. Let $v \in V(K(n,k,\geqslant t))$, and let $K \in \binom{[n]}{k}$ be the corresponding $k$-subset. The number of subsets in $\binom{[n]}{s}$ that intersect $K$ at exactly $i$ elements is $\binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{s-i}$. Therefore, there are $ \sum_{i=t+r}^{t+2r} \binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{s-i} $ subsets $S \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $t + r \leqslant |K \cap S| \leqslant t + 2r$. For each such subset $S$, note that $K \in \mathcal{F}_{n,k,t,r}^S$. Therefore, each vertex $v \in V(K(n,k,\geqslant t))$ is in $\sum_{i=t+r}^{t+2r} \binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{s-i}$ cliques of $\mathcal{K}$. By \cref{lem:equiv_frac}, \begin{align*} \theta_f(K(n,k,\geqslant t)) & \leqslant \frac{\binom{n}{s}}{\sum_{i=t+r}^{t+2r} \binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{s-i}}. \end{align*} Note that \begin{align*} \frac{\binom{n}{s}}{\binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{s-i}} & = \frac{i! (k-i)! (s-i)! (n-k-s+i)! n!}{k! (n-k)! s! (n-s)!} = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{s}{i} \binom{n-s}{k-i}}. \end{align*} Consequently, \begin{align*} \theta_f(K(n,k,\geqslant t)) & \leqslant \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\sum_{i=t+r}^{t+2r} \binom{s}{i} \binom{n-s}{k-i}} = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{f_{n,k,t}}, \end{align*} where we have used \cref{eq:frac} for the last equality. Since $\alpha(G) \chi_f(G) \geqslant |V(G)|$ for every graph $G$, by \cref{thm:akt}, $\chi_f(\overline{K(n,k,\geqslant t)}) \geqslant \binom{n}{k} / f_{n,k,t}$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound by covering with all translates $\mathcal{F}^S$ and Lemma 2.23 plus a binomial identity; lower bound from $\alpha\chi_f\ge|V|$ and Theorem 3.47.

nodes.name: HC for inflations of generalised Kneser graphs with large cliques
nodes.statement: Let $n, k, t \geqslant 1$ be integers with $2k - t \leqslant n < 3k - 3t + 3$. If $ f_{n,k,t} \geqslant \left(\frac{1}{4} + \varepsilon\right) \binom{n}{k}, $ where $\varepsilon:=1/62$, then any inflation of $K(n, k, \geqslant t)$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
assumptions: $n, k, t \geqslant 1$ be integers with $2k - t \leqslant n < 3k - 3t + 3$
conclusions: any inflation of $K(n, k, \geqslant t)$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}
nodes.label: thm:generalised_kneser_graphs

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.49
nodes.statement: By \cref{thm:fractional_kneser_graphs}, $\theta_f(K(n,k,\geqslant t)) = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{f_{n,k,t}} \leqslant 1/(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{62}) = 124/33$. By \cref{thm:124/33}, any inflation of $K(n, k, \geqslant t)$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.48 gives $\theta_f\le 124/33$; apply Theorem 2.32.

nodes.name: odd girth
nodes.statement: The \defn{odd girth} of a graph $G$ is the length of the shortest odd cycle in $G$.

nodes.name: Denley's odd girth of generalised Kneser graphs
nodes.statement: For integers $n, k, t \geqslant 1$, the odd girth of the generalised Kneser graph $K(n,k, \leqslant t)$ is $ 2 \left\lceil\frac{k-t}{n - 2(k-t)} \right\rceil + 1. $
conclusions: the odd girth of the generalised Kneser graph $K(n,k, \leqslant t)$ is $ 2 \left\lceil\frac{k-t}{n - 2(k-t)} \right\rceil + 1
nodes.label: thm:odd_girth_of_kneser_graph

nodes.name: CDM for inflations of K(n,k,>=t+1) with large odd girth complement
nodes.statement: For integers $n,k,t \geqslant 1$ with $2k - t \leqslant n < \frac{5}{2} (k-t)$, any inflation $G$ of $K(n, k,\geqslant t+1)$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}.
also_stated_at: For integers $n,k,t \geqslant 1$ with $2k - t \leqslant n < \frac{5}{2} (k-t)$, any inflation $G$ of $K(n, k,\geqslant t+1)$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}
nodes.label: thm:generalised_kneser_graphs2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.51
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an inflation of $K(n, k,\geqslant t+1)$. Since $2k - t \leqslant n < \frac{5}{2} (k-t)$, by \cref{thm:odd_girth_of_kneser_graph}, the odd girth of $K(n,k, \leqslant t)$ is at least $7$. Therefore, $K(n, k,\leqslant t)$ is $C_5$-free. Since $C_5$ is adjacent-twin-free, and since $\overline{C_5} \cong C_5$, by \cref{lem:blow_up_avoidant}, $G$ is $C_5$-free. By \cref{thm:c5}, $C_5$ is \nameref{conj:cdm}-unavoidable. Therefore, $G$ satisfies \nameref{conj:cdm}.
nodes.statement_short: Odd girth $\ge 7$ (Theorem 3.50) makes the complement $C_5$-free; inflation preserves this (Lemma 2.18) and Theorem 2.15 applies.

nodes.name: (lambda,mu)-strongly regular
nodes.statement: For integers $\lambda \geqslant 0$ and $\mu \geqslant 1$, a $k$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is \defn{$(\lambda ,\mu)$-strongly regular} if every pair of adjacent vertices has $\lambda$ common neighbours, and every pair of distinct non-adjacent vertices has $\mu$ common neighbours.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs

nodes.name: srg notation
nodes.statement: Our notation for such a graph is \defn{$\mathrm{srg}(n, k, \lambda, \mu)$}.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs

nodes.name: strongly regular graph
nodes.statement: A regular graph is \defn{strongly regular} if it is $(\lambda, \mu)$-strongly regular for some integers $\lambda \geqslant 0$ and $\mu \geqslant 1$.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs

nodes.name: trivial strongly regular triangle-free graphs
nodes.statement: Complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$ are \defn{trivial} examples.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs

nodes.name: Infinitely many triangle-free strongly regular graphs?
nodes.statement: It is open whether infinitely many non-trivial triangle-free strongly regular graphs exist \citep{devillers2024triangle}.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs

nodes.name: Biggs: finitely many (0,mu)-strongly regular graphs
nodes.statement: \citet{Biggs71a} showed that for any $\mu \notin \{2, 4, 6\}$, only finitely many $(0, \mu)$-strongly regular graphs exist; see \citep{Biggs09a,Biggs09,Biggs11,Elzinga03} for related results.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs
conclusions: only finitely many $(0, \mu)$-strongly regular graphs exist

nodes.name: Xu et al.: HC for complements of Clebsch and Petersen graphs
nodes.statement: \citet{xu_hadwigers_2025} proved Hadwiger's Conjecture for the complement of the Clebsch and Petersen graphs.
nodes.section: 3.3 Complements of Strongly Regular Triangle-Free Graphs
conclusions: Hadwiger's Conjecture for the complement of the Clebsch and Petersen graphs

nodes.name: hypercube
nodes.statement: For an integer $n \geqslant 1$, an \defn{$n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$} is the graph whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$, with two vertices adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate.

nodes.name: opposite vertices
nodes.statement: Two vertices are \defn{opposite} in an $n$-dimensional hypercube if their corresponding vectors differ in all $n$ coordinates.

nodes.name: Clebsch graph
nodes.statement: The \defn{Clebsch graph} is obtained from a $4$-dimensional hypercube by adding edges between all pairs of opposite vertices. It is a strongly regular graph with parameters $\mathrm{srg}(16,5,0,2)$ \citep{Clebsch}.

nodes.name: Fractional clique covering number of the complement of the Clebsch graph
nodes.statement: If $G$ is the complement of the Clebsch graph, then $\theta_f(G) \leqslant 16/5$.
assumptions: $G$ is the complement of the Clebsch graph
nodes.label: lem:fraction_clebsch

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.52
nodes.statement: For each vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $S_v = V(G) \setminus (N_G(v) \cup \{v\})$. Since $G$ is $10$-regular, $|S_v| = 5$. Since $\alpha(G) = 2$, each $S_v$ is a clique in $G$. Each vertex $w \in V(G)$ is in exactly $5$ of $\{S_v : v \in V(G)\}$, corresponding to the $5$ non-neighbours of $v$ in $G$. By \cref{lem:equiv_frac}, $\theta_f(G) \leqslant 16/5$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-neighbourhoods $S_v$ are 16 cliques covering each vertex 5 times; apply Lemma 2.23.

nodes.name: HC for inflations of the complement of the Clebsch graph
nodes.statement: Every inflation of the complement of the Clebsch graph satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
assumptions: inflation of the complement of the Clebsch graph
nodes.label: lem:inflation_clebsch

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.53
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an inflation of the complement of the Clebsch graph. By \cref{cor:inflation_frac,lem:fraction_clebsch}, $\theta_f(G) \leqslant 16/5 < 124/33$. \cref{thm:124/33} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_f\le16/5<124/33$ by Corollary 2.25 and Lemma 3.52; apply Theorem 2.32.

nodes.name: Steiner system
nodes.statement: A \defn{Steiner system} with parameters $t, k, n \geqslant 1$, denoted $\mathdefn{S(t,k,n)}$, is a family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$, called \defn{blocks}, such that each $t$-element subset of $[n]$ is contained in exactly one block.

nodes.name: Number of blocks of a Steiner system
nodes.statement: The total number of $t$-element subsets of $[n]$ is $\binom{n}{t}$, and each block contains $\binom{k}{t}$ of these subsets. Since each $t$-subset is contained in exactly one block, the number of blocks is $\binom{n}{t}/\binom{k}{t}$.

nodes.name: Mesner graph
nodes.statement: The \defn{Mesner graph}, or the \defn{$M_{22}$} graph, is the unique graph generated by the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$. Its vertices correspond to the blocks of the Steiner system, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if their corresponding blocks are disjoint. It is a strongly regular graph with parameters $\mathrm{srg}(77, 16, 0, 4)$ \citep{Mesner}.

nodes.name: M22 contains all known unavoidable graphs
nodes.statement: We verified computationally that $M_{22}$ contains every graph in \cref{tab:unavoidable_graphs} as an induced subgraph, so one cannot apply the techniques described in \cref{ss:induced}.
conclusions: $M_{22}$ contains every graph in \cref{tab:unavoidable_graphs} as an induced subgraph

nodes.name: Fractional clique covering number of the complement of the Mesner graph
nodes.statement: $\theta_f(\overline{{M}_{22}}) \leqslant 22/6$.
nodes.label: fractional_m22

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.54
nodes.statement: For each $i \in \{1, \dots, 22\}$, let $\mathcal{S}_i \subseteq V(\overline{{M}_{22}})$ be the set of vertices corresponding to blocks containing $i$. Then $\mathcal{S}_i$ is a clique in $\overline{M_{22}}$. Each vertex of $\overline{M_{22}}$ is in exactly $6$ of these cliques. \cref{lem:equiv_frac} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: The 22 point-stars of $S(3,6,22)$ are cliques covering each vertex 6 times; apply Lemma 2.23.

nodes.name: HC for inflations of the complement of the Mesner graph
nodes.statement: Every inflation of $\overline{M_{22}}$ satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
nodes.label: lem:inflation_m22

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.55
nodes.statement: By \cref{fractional_m22}, $\theta_f(\overline{M}_{22}) \leqslant 22/6 < 124/33$. \cref{thm:124/33} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_f\le 22/6<124/33$ by Theorem 3.54; apply Theorem 2.32.

nodes.name: Gewirtz graph
nodes.statement: The Gewirtz graph is constructed as follows. Consider the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$ defined in \cref{sss:mesner}. Choose an element of $\{1, \dots, 22\}$, and let the vertices of the Gewirtz graph be the blocks not containing this element. Two blocks are adjacent if and only if they are disjoint. The Gewirtz graph is strongly regular with parameters $\mathrm{srg}(56, 10, 0, 2)$ \citep{Gewirtz}.

nodes.name: Gewirtz graph is an induced subgraph of the Mesner graph
nodes.statement: By construction, the Gewirtz graph is an induced subgraph of the Mesner graph. Therefore, an inflation of the complement of the Gewirtz graph is an inflation of the complement of the Mesner graph.
conclusions: the Gewirtz graph is an induced subgraph of the Mesner graph
an inflation of the complement of the Gewirtz graph is an inflation of the complement of the Mesner graph

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.56
nodes.statement: \cref{cor:gewirtz} follows directly from \cref{lem:inflation_m22}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Lemma 3.55 since Gewirtz inflations are Mesner inflations.

nodes.name: HC for inflations of the complement of the Gewirtz graph
nodes.statement: Every inflation of the complement of the Gewirtz graph satisfies \nameref{conj:hc_chi}.
assumptions: inflation of the complement of the Gewirtz graph
nodes.label: cor:gewirtz

nodes.name: Higman-Sims graph
nodes.statement: The Higman-Sims graph, introduced by \citet{higman1968simple}, is constructed by slightly modifying the Mesner graph. Take the Mesner graph described in \cref{sss:mesner} and add $22$ new vertices, each corresponding to an element of $\{1, \dots, 22\}$. Each new vertex is adjacent to a block in $M_{22}$ if its corresponding element is in the block. Finally, add a vertex adjacent to all $22$ new vertices. It is a strong regular graph with parameters $\mathrm{srg}(100, 22, 0, 6)$ \citep{HigmanSims}.

nodes.name: Chromatic and clique numbers of the complement of Higman-Sims
nodes.statement: Its complement has chromatic number $50$ and clique number $22$.
conclusions: Its complement has chromatic number $50$ and clique number $22$

nodes.name: Existing tools fail for the Higman-Sims complement
nodes.statement: Due to the small size of the clique number relative to the order of the graph, \cref{thm:icr1/4} or \cref{thm:fcc} cannot be applied to prove Hadwiger's Conjecture for inflations of the complement of the Higman-Sims graph. Moreover, we computationally checked that the Higman-Sims graph contains every graph in \cref{tab:unavoidable_graphs} as an induced subgraph.

nodes.name: Computational proof for the Higman-Sims complement
nodes.statement_short: Explicit $K_{50}$-model with 50 branch sets of size 2, found by computer (SageMath labelling).

nodes.name: SHC_{n/2} for the complement of the Higman-Sims graph
nodes.statement: The complement of the Higman-Sims graph satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}.
also_stated_at: The complement of the Higman-Sims graph satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}
conclusions: The complement of the Higman-Sims graph satisfies \nameref{conj:shc_half}
nodes.label: thm:higman_sims

nodes.name: Wood's conjecture on triangle-free diameter-2 graphs
nodes.statement: For every integer $t \geqslant 2$, there exists an integer $n_0$ such that if $G$ is a triangle-free diameter $2$ graph that does not contain $K_{2,t}$ as a subgraph with $n \geqslant n_0$ vertices, then $G$ is the star graph $K_{1, n-1}$.
assumptions: $G$ is a triangle-free diameter $2$ graph that does not contain $K_{2,t}$ as a subgraph with $n \geqslant n_0$ vertices
nodes.label: conj:wood
